```{r helpers-gfw}
load_object <- function(filepath, object_name = NULL) {
  local({
    e <- new.env()
    load(filepath, envir = e)
    if (is.null(object_name)) {
      objects <- ls(e)
      if (length(objects) == 1) {
        e[[objects]]
      } else {
        stop("File contains ", length(objects), " objects (",
             paste(objects, collapse=", "),
             "). Please specify object_name.")
      }
    } else {
      e[[object_name]]
    }
  })
}

# msg() — like message() but flushes immediately to the RStudio console.
# Useful when running chunks interactively: without flush.console(), messages
# from inside long-running blocks are buffered and only appear after the block
# completes, making it look like nothing is happening.
msg <- function(...) {
  message(...)
  flush.console()
}

apply_flag_other <- function(df, flag_col = "vessel_flag",
                              days_col = "fishing_days") {
  df %>%
    group_by(across(all_of(flag_col))) %>%
    mutate(total_flag_days = sum(.data[[days_col]])) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(
      total_days = sum(.data[[days_col]]),
      flag_pct   = total_flag_days / total_days * 100,
      across(all_of(flag_col),
             ~ if_else(flag_pct < threshold_pct, "Other", .x))
    )
}
```

map_gear_aer <- function(x) {
  dplyr::recode(str_to_upper(str_trim(x)),
    DTS = "Bottom trawl/seine", TBB = "Beam trawl",
    PEL = "Midwater trawl",     DFN = "Gillnet",

# Species group lookup — used in multiple landings plots
assign_species_group <- function(species_code, species_name) {
  sn <- tolower(species_name)
  case_when(
    # ---- Pelagic fish -------------------------------------------------------
    str_detect(sn, "herring|sardine|pilchard") |
      species_code %in% c("HER","PIL","SPR","SAR","SIH") |
      str_detect(sn, "^mackerel") |
      species_code %in% c("MAC","MAS") |
      str_detect(sn, "horse mackerel|scad") |
      species_code %in% c("HOM","HMM","JAA","JAX")
      ~ "Pelagic fish",

    # ---- Seaweeds -----------------------------------------------------------
    str_detect(sn, "seaweed|kelp|tangle|laminaria|fucus|ulva|algae|alga|macroalg") |
      species_code %in% c("LQD","LAH","SWX","SWA","SWB","SWC","SWD","SWE",
                           "SWF","SWG","SWH","SWI","SWJ","SWK","SWL","SWM",
                           "SWN","SWO","SWP","SWQ","SWR","SWS","SWT","SWU",
                           "SWV","SWT","SWW","ASP","ULV","FUC","LAM","ALG")
      ~ "Seaweeds",

    # ---- Cephalopods --------------------------------------------------------
    str_detect(sn, "cuttlefish|sepia") |
      species_code %in% c("CTC","CTL","CTZ","CTB","CTS","SEB","OCC")
      ~ "Cuttlefish",
    
    str_detect(sn, "squid|loligo|bobtail|ommastrep|shortfin") |
      species_code %in% c("SQC","SQR","SQE","SQM","LOL","LOG","SQS","SQZ",
                           "SQX","EUR","BOC","SQI","OMS","TOD","NBS","OMP","ILL")
      ~ "Squid",

    # ---- Demersal fish ------------------------------------------------------
    str_detect(sn, "mullet") |
      species_code %in% c("MUL","MUG","TFM","MUT","MUX")
      ~ "Mullets",
    
    str_detect(sn, "gurnard|searobin") |
      species_code %in% c("GUG","GUR","GUU","GUX","TUB","BIR")
      ~ "Gurnards",
    
    str_detect(sn, "whiting|haddock|cod") |
      species_code %in% c("WHG","HAD", "COD")
      ~ "Roundfish",
    
    species_code %in% c(
      "SOL","SOM","SOO","SOZ",
      "PLE",
      "TUR","BLL",
      "DAB","FLE",
      "MEG","LDB","MES",
      "LEM","WIT","SCL","POO",
      "HAL","GHL",
      "SXS","CET",
      "FLX","FLO","BUT","RHG"
    ) |
    str_detect(sn, "plaice|\\bsole\\b|turbot|brill|\\bdab\\b|flounder|halibut|megrim|witch|limande|cardine|fletan|plie|pliee")
      ~ "Flatfishes",

    # ---- Shellfish & invertebrates ------------------------------------------
    str_detect(sn, "scallop|pecten") |
      species_code %in% c("SCE","QSC","PEC","SCA","SCB")
      ~ "Scallops",
    str_detect(sn, "shrimp|crangon|pandalus|crevette") |
      species_code %in% c("CSH","PRA","TGS","CRG","CPR","SQS","PAN","CFW")
      ~ "Shrimps",
    
    # ---- Other shellfish & crustaceans --------------------------------------
    str_detect(sn, "whelk|buccin|crab|lobster|crawfish|langoustine|nepthrops|venus|mussel|clam|cockle|oyster") |
      species_code %in% c("WHE","BUC","CRE","SCR","LBE","NEP","VEV",
                           "MYV","MYE","COC","OYF","OYG","CLX","SCX")
      ~ "Shellfish & crustaceans",

    # ---- Other demersal fish ------------------------------------------------
    str_detect(sn, "seabream|seabass|bass|bream|pouting|bib|pollack|pollock|conger|catshark|smooth.hound|ray|skate|shark|dogfish") |
      species_code %in% c("BRB","BSS","BIB","POL","COE","SYC","SDV",
                           "RJC","RJH","RJB","RJN","RJM","RJI","SKA",
                           "DGS","DGH","SCK","SDS","GKL","MZZ")
      ~ "Other demersal fish",
    TRUE ~ NA_character_
  )
}

# ---- Pelagic data anomaly flag ----------------------------------------------
# NLD VL40XX Other/mixed pelagic landings in 27.4.C in 2012 are anomalously
# high (~84,000 t vs ~10,000 t in surrounding years), consistent with a
# sub-region misattribution in the AER source data (Channel landings apparently
# reported under 27.4.C rather than 27.7.D). Requires verification with STECF/CBS.
pelagic_species_codes <- c("HER","PIL","HOM","MAC","SPR","JAX","HMM","JAA","MAS","SAR","SIH")

pelagic_anomaly_note <- paste0(
  "* 2012 NLD pelagic landings in 27.4.C excluded due to anomalously high values ",
  "Requires verification with STECF/AER."
)

remove_pelagic_anomaly <- function(df) {
  df |>
    filter(!(country_code  == "NLD"         &
             sub_reg       == "27.4.c"      &
             year          == 2012          &
             gear_category == "Other/mixed" &
             species_code  %in% pelagic_species_codes))
}

```{r helpers-fdi}
safe_numeric <- function(x, extra_sentinels = character(0)) {
  base_pat <- "NK|na|N/A|#N/A|CONFID|confidential|BEL|\\."
  full_pat  <- if (length(extra_sentinels) > 0)
    paste0("^(", base_pat, "|", paste(extra_sentinels, collapse = "|"), ")$")
  else
    paste0("^(", base_pat, ")$")
  cleaned <- str_trim(x) |>
    str_replace_all(regex(full_pat, ignore_case = TRUE), NA_character_)
  val <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(cleaned))
  val[!is.na(val) & val == -1] <- NA_real_
  val
}

normalise_division <- function(x) {
  x <- str_trim(x) |> str_to_upper()
  x <- str_remove(x, "^27\\.")
  str_replace(x, "^(\\d+)([A-Z])$", "\\1.\\2")
}

map_gear_fdi <- function(gear_code) {
  lookup <- c(
    OTB="Bottom trawl", OTT="Bottom trawl", PTB="Bottom trawl",
    OTM="Midwater trawl", PTM="Midwater trawl",
    TBB="Beam trawl",
    SSC="Scottish seine", SDN="Danish seine",
    GNS="Gillnet", GND="Gillnet",
    FPN="Pot/trap", FPO="Pot/trap",
    LLS="Longline", LLD="Longline",
    DRB="Dredge",
    MIS="Other/mixed", NK="Unknown"
  )
  dplyr::recode(str_to_upper(str_trim(gear_code)),
                !!!lookup, .default = "Other/mixed")
}

```{r table_helpers}

# ---- Shared flextable style -------------------------------------------------
# Call this on any flextable to apply consistent report formatting.
# Adjust font, size and colours once here; all tables update automatically.

style_ft <- function(ft, font_size = 6, font_name = "Calibri") {
  n_rows <- nrow(ft$body$dataset)

  ft |>
    flextable::font(fontname = font_name, part = "all") |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = font_size,     part = "body") |>
    flextable::fontsize(size = font_size + 1, part = "header") |>
    flextable::bold(part = "header") |>
    flextable::bold(j = 1,      part = "body") |>        # bold row label column
    flextable::bold(i = n_rows, part = "body") |>        # bold Total row
    flextable::bg(part = "header", bg = "#D9E1F2") |>
    flextable::bg(i = n_rows, part = "body", bg = "#F2F2F2") |>
    flextable::hline_top(part = "header",
                         border = officer::fp_border(width = 1.5)) |>
    flextable::hline_bottom(part = "header",
                            border = officer::fp_border(width = 1)) |>
    flextable::hline_bottom(part = "body",
                            border = officer::fp_border(width = 1.5)) |>
    flextable::colformat_num(big.mark = ",", digits = 0) |>
    flextable::set_table_properties(layout = "autofit", width = 1) |>
    flextable::align(j = -1, align = "right", part = "all") |>
    flextable::align(j = 1,  align = "left",  part = "all")
}

# ---- Shared table builder ---------------------------------------------------
make_annex_table <- function(df, row_var, col_var, value_var,
                              row_label  = row_var,
                              col_levels = NULL,
                              other_label   = "Other",
                              add_other     = TRUE,
                              add_total_row = TRUE,
                              add_total_col = TRUE,
                              caption       = NULL,
                              font_size     = 8) {

  # Lump unlisted categories into "Other"
  if (add_other && !is.null(col_levels)) {
    df <- df |>
      mutate(!!col_var := if_else(
        .data[[col_var]] %in% col_levels,
        .data[[col_var]], other_label))
  }

  # Summarise and pivot wide
  wide <- df |>
    group_by(.data[[row_var]], .data[[col_var]]) |>
    summarise(val = sum(.data[[value_var]], na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
    mutate(val = round(val)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from  = all_of(col_var),
                values_from = val,
                values_fill = 0L)

  # Order columns: specified levels first, then Other if present
  col_order <- if (!is.null(col_levels)) {
    present <- col_levels[col_levels %in% names(wide)]
    other_present <- if (add_other && other_label %in% names(wide))
      other_label else character(0)
    c(present, other_present)
  } else {
    setdiff(names(wide), row_var)
  }
  wide <- wide |> dplyr::select(all_of(c(row_var, col_order)))

  # Total column
  num_cols <- col_order   # all non-row columns at this point
  if (add_total_col) {
    wide <- wide |>
      mutate(Total = rowSums(across(all_of(num_cols)), na.rm = TRUE))
    num_cols <- c(num_cols, "Total")
  }

  # Total row — coerce row_var to character to avoid type clash in bind_rows
  if (add_total_row) {
    total_row <- wide |>
      summarise(across(all_of(num_cols), \(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
      mutate(!!row_var := "Total")          # character; matches after coercion below
    wide <- wide |>
      mutate(!!row_var := as.character(.data[[row_var]])) |>  # coerce before bind
      bind_rows(total_row)
  }

  # Rename row label column
  names(wide)[1] <- row_label

  # Build flextable
  ft <- flextable::flextable(wide) |>
    style_ft(font_size = font_size)

  if (!is.null(caption)) {
    ft <- flextable::set_caption(ft, caption = caption)
  }

  ft
}

```

```{r load-aer}
# Cache: cache_aer.RData — five objects, all pre-filtered to study_divisions_aer:
#   aer_effort_raw              (wide, one row per stratum)
#   aer_effort_summary          (aggregated by year/country/gear/sub_reg/vessel_length)
#   aer_effort_capacity_metric  (adds gt_fishdays_source + gt_fishdays_harmonised)
#   aer_landings_raw            (wide, one row per stratum × species)
#   aer_landings_summary        (aggregated by year/country/gear/sub_reg/species)
#
# Cache is invalidated when:
#   (a) the raw AER Excel file is newer than the cache, OR
#   (b) the cache exists but is missing any of the five expected objects
#       (handles caches built before an object was added)

aer_raw_mtime   <- file.mtime(aer_file)
aer_cache_mtime <- if (file.exists(aer_cache)) file.mtime(aer_cache) else as.POSIXct(0)

# Check (b): peek at saved object names without loading into global environment
aer_required_objects <- c("aer_effort_raw", "aer_effort_summary",
                           "aer_effort_capacity_metric",
                           "aer_landings_raw", "aer_landings_summary")
aer_cache_complete <- if (file.exists(aer_cache)) {
  all(aer_required_objects %in% load(aer_cache, envir = new.env()))
} else {
  FALSE
}

if (aer_cache_mtime > aer_raw_mtime && aer_cache_complete) {

  msg("AER: loading from cache (", format(aer_cache_mtime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), ")")
  load(aer_cache)

} else {

  if (!aer_cache_complete)
    msg("AER: cache incomplete (missing objects) — rebuilding ...")
  else
    msg("AER: cache stale — reading raw Excel file ...")

  aer_effort_sheet <- read_excel(aer_file, sheet = "FS_effort by sub-region ") |>
    clean_names()
  msg("AER effort sheet: ", nrow(aer_effort_sheet), " rows, ",
          ncol(aer_effort_sheet), " columns")
  msg("  variable_code values: ",
          paste(sort(unique(aer_effort_sheet$variable_code)), collapse=", "))
  msg("  sub_reg values (sample): ",
          paste(head(sort(unique(aer_effort_sheet$sub_reg)), 20), collapse=", "))

  aer_effort_raw <- aer_effort_sheet |>
    filter(!is.na(variable_code), !is.na(value)) |>
    mutate(
      year          = as.integer(year),
      sub_reg       = str_to_lower(str_trim(sub_reg)),
      gear_category = map_gear_aer(fishing_tech)
    ) |>
    # Filter to study area BEFORE pivot to reduce size
    filter(sub_reg %in% study_divisions_aer) |>
    # NOTE: fs_name is intentionally excluded from the pivot keys.
    # It is a free-text fleet segment label that can differ across rows of the
    # same stratum, which would create spurious extra rows if included.
    # year + country_code + sub_reg + fishing_tech + vessel_length + gear_category
    # form the natural stratum key; values_fn = sum handles any remaining
    # duplicates within a stratum × variable_code combination.
    dplyr::select(year, country_code, sub_reg, fishing_tech,
           vessel_length, gear_category,
           variable_code, value) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = variable_code, values_from = value,
                values_fn = sum)

  msg("AER effort after pivot (study area): ", nrow(aer_effort_raw), " rows")
  msg("  Columns: ", paste(names(aer_effort_raw), collapse=", "))
  msg("  Countries: ", paste(sort(unique(aer_effort_raw$country_code)), collapse=", "))
  msg("  Year range: ", min(aer_effort_raw$year), "–", max(aer_effort_raw$year))

  aer_landings_sheets <- bind_rows(
    read_excel(aer_file, sheet = "FS_landings FAO 2008-2012") |> clean_names(),
    read_excel(aer_file, sheet = "FS_landings FAO 2013-2017") |> clean_names(),
    read_excel(aer_file, sheet = "FS_landings FAO 2018-2023") |> clean_names()
  )
  msg("AER landings sheets combined: ", nrow(aer_landings_sheets), " rows")

  aer_landings_raw <- aer_landings_sheets |>
    filter(!is.na(variable_code), !is.na(value)) |>
    mutate(
      year          = as.integer(year),
      sub_reg       = str_to_lower(str_trim(sub_reg)),
      gear_category = map_gear_aer(fishing_tech)
    ) |>
    # Filter to study area BEFORE pivot
    filter(sub_reg %in% study_divisions_aer) |>
    dplyr::select(year, country_code, sub_reg, fishing_tech,
           vessel_length, gear_category,
           species_code, species_name,
           variable_code, value) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = variable_code, values_from = value,
                values_fn = sum) |>
    rename(live_weight_kg = totwghtlandg,
           value_euro     = totvallandg) |>
    mutate(live_weight_t = live_weight_kg / 1000)

  msg("AER landings after pivot (study area): ", nrow(aer_landings_raw), " rows")
  msg("  Countries: ", paste(sort(unique(aer_landings_raw$country_code)), collapse=", "))

  # Basic fishing-days summary — retains vessel_length for capacity plot
  aer_effort_summary <- aer_effort_raw |>
    group_by(year, country_code, gear_category, sub_reg, vessel_length) |>
    summarise(
      across(any_of(c("totfishdays","totseadays","totkwfishdays","totgtfishdays")),
             ~ sum(.x, na.rm = TRUE)),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # Capacity-weighted effort: GT-fishing days where available; impute from
  # kW-fishing days for countries that only report kW (using fleet-average ratio).
  # A flag column records the source so plots can distinguish imputed values.
  aer_effort_capacity_metric <- aer_effort_summary |>
    mutate(
      gt_fishdays_source = case_when(
        totgtfishdays > 0             ~ "GT (reported)",
        totkwfishdays > 0             ~ "GT (imputed from kW)",
        TRUE                          ~ "Not available"
      ),
      gt_fishdays_harmonised = case_when(
        totgtfishdays > 0             ~ totgtfishdays,
        totkwfishdays > 0             ~ totkwfishdays * kw_to_gt_ratio,
        TRUE                          ~ NA_real_
      )
    )

  aer_landings_summary <- aer_landings_raw |>
    group_by(year, country_code, gear_category,
             sub_reg, species_code, species_name) |>
    summarise(
      live_weight_t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm = TRUE),
      value_euro    = sum(value_euro,    na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  # Both raw objects are already filtered to study_divisions_aer above,
  # so the cache contains only study-area rows — no further filtering needed.
  save(aer_effort_raw, aer_effort_summary, aer_effort_capacity_metric,
       aer_landings_raw, aer_landings_summary,
       file = aer_cache)
  msg("AER: cache saved → ", aer_cache)

  
  
  # aer_landings_sheets <- bind_rows(
  #   read_excel(aer_file, sheet = "FS_landings FAO 2008-2012") |> clean_names(),
  #   read_excel(aer_file, sheet = "FS_landings FAO 2013-2017") |> clean_names(),
  #   read_excel(aer_file, sheet = "FS_landings FAO 2018-2023") |> clean_names()
  # )  
  
  # aer_landings_sheets %>% 
  #   filter(species_code == "HER") %>% 
  #   filter(country_code == "NLD") %>% 
  #   filter(variable_code == "totwghtlandg") %>% 
  #   filter(sub_reg %in% c("27.4.a","27.4.b", "27.4.c","27.7.d")) %>% 
  #   group_by(species_name, year, sub_reg) %>% 
  #   summarise(total_t = sum(value)/1000) %>% 
  #   ggplot(aes(x=year, y=total_t, fill=sub_reg)) +
  #   geom_col(position="stack", width=0.8, na.rm=TRUE) 
    
  # rm(aer_landings_sheets)
  
}

```{r load-gfw}

gfw_cache_mtime <- if (file.exists(gfw_cache)) file.mtime(gfw_cache) else as.POSIXct(0)

# Only stat the source files if the cache doesn't exist — avoids slow
# network/OneDrive lookups on every knit when the cache is warm.
gfw_cache_valid <- if (file.exists(gfw_cache)) {
  gfw_raw_mtime <- max(file.mtime(c(
    file.path(flyshootdir, "gfw_s7_effort.RData"),
    file.path(flyshootdir, "gfw_s6_zones.RData"),
    file.path(flyshootdir, "gfw_s3_vessel_meta.RData")
  )), na.rm = TRUE)
  gfw_cache_mtime > gfw_raw_mtime
} else {
  FALSE
}

if (gfw_cache_valid) {
  msg("GFW: loading from cache (", format(gfw_cache_mtime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), ")")
  load(gfw_cache)
} else {
  msg("GFW: cache missing or stale — loading pipeline RData files ...")
  fishing_days_study   <- load_object(
    file.path(flyshootdir, "gfw_s7_effort.RData"), "fishing_days_study")
  events_classified_fr <- load_object(
    file.path(flyshootdir, "gfw_s6_zones.RData"), "events_classified_fr")
  vessel_meta          <- load_object(
    file.path(flyshootdir, "gfw_s3_vessel_meta.RData"), "vessel_meta")
  world   <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf")
  fao_sf  <- load_object(file.path(spatialdir, "fao_sf.RData"), "fao_sf")
  fao_sf_division <- fao_sf |>
    filter(F_LEVEL == "DIVISION") |>
    dplyr::select(division = F_DIVISION) |>
    mutate(division = toupper(division)) |>
    filter(division %in% study_divisions_gfw) |>
    group_by(division) |>
    summarise(geometry = st_union(geometry)) |>
    st_make_valid()
  rm(fao_sf)
  save(fishing_days_study, events_classified_fr, vessel_meta,
       fao_sf_division, world,
       file = gfw_cache)
  msg("GFW: cache saved → ", gfw_cache)
}

```{r load-gfw-spatial}
# Cache: cache_gfw_spatial.RData
# Stores all expensive computed spatial objects so they survive across knits.
# Objects saved:
#   land_study, study_window_proj, study_owin,
#   world_proj, fao_div_proj,
#   bbox_7d_proj, window_7d_proj, window_7d_owin,
#   kde_results      (all-area KDE, all years)
#   kde_7d           (7D KDE, all years)
#   cell_effort_7d   (events per 5 km cell per year, 7D)
#   cell_effort_full (full grid with zeros, 7D)
#   concentration_7d (Gini + top10 per year, 7D)
#
# To force recomputation (e.g. after new GFW data):
#   file.remove(spatial_cache)

crs_proj    <- 32630
sigma_all   <- 20000   # KDE bandwidth for all-area map (m)
sigma_7d    <- 10000   # KDE bandwidth for 7D map (m)
kde_sample  <- 10000   # events sampled per year for KDE
cell_size   <- 5000    # grid cell size for concentration (m)

spatial_cache_mtime <- if (file.exists(spatial_cache)) file.mtime(spatial_cache) else as.POSIXct(0)
gfw_cache_mtime_now <- file.mtime(gfw_cache)   # spatial depends on gfw objects

if (spatial_cache_mtime > gfw_cache_mtime_now) {

  msg("GFW spatial: loading from cache (", format(spatial_cache_mtime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), ")")
  load(spatial_cache)

} else {

  msg("GFW spatial: computing spatial objects (this takes a few minutes) ...")

  # ---- Base spatial objects ------------------------------------------------
  land_study <- world %>%
    st_crop(st_bbox(c(xmin = xlim[1], xmax = xlim[2],
                      ymin = ylim[1], ymax = ylim[2]), crs = 4326)) %>%
    st_union()

  study_window_sf <- fao_sf_division %>%
    st_union() %>%
    st_difference(land_study) %>%
    st_make_valid()

  study_window_proj <- study_window_sf %>% st_transform(crs_proj)
  study_owin        <- as.owin(study_window_proj)
  world_proj        <- world           %>% st_transform(crs_proj)
  fao_div_proj      <- fao_sf_division %>% st_transform(crs_proj)

  # ---- 7D spatial objects --------------------------------------------------
  bbox_7d <- st_bbox(fao_sf_division %>% filter(division == "27.7.D"))
  land_7d <- world %>% st_crop(bbox_7d) %>% st_union()
  window_7d_sf <- fao_sf_division %>%
    filter(division == "27.7.D") %>%
    st_difference(land_7d) %>%
    st_make_valid()
  window_7d_proj <- window_7d_sf %>% st_transform(crs_proj)
  window_7d_owin <- as.owin(window_7d_proj)
  bbox_7d_proj   <- st_bbox(window_7d_proj)

  # ---- KDE — all divisions -------------------------------------------------
  events_for_kde_proj <- events_classified_fr %>%
    mutate(year = lubridate::year(start)) %>%
    filter(year %in% study_years, !is.na(lon), !is.na(lat)) %>%
    dplyr::select(year, lon, lat) %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    slice_sample(n = kde_sample) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    st_as_sf(coords = c("lon","lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
    st_transform(crs_proj) %>%
    mutate(x = st_coordinates(.)[,1], y = st_coordinates(.)[,2]) %>%
    st_drop_geometry()

  kde_results <- map_dfr(study_years, function(yr) {
    pts <- events_for_kde_proj %>% filter(year == yr)
    if (nrow(pts) < 50) return(NULL)
    ppp_yr <- tryCatch(
      ppp(x = pts$x, y = pts$y, window = study_owin),
      error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(ppp_yr)) return(NULL)
    kde <- density(ppp_yr, sigma = sigma_all, dimyx = c(200,200), edge = TRUE)
    as.data.frame(kde) %>%
      rename(x=x, y=y, density=value) %>%
      filter(!is.na(density), density > 0) %>%
      mutate(ndensity = density / max(density), year = yr)
  })

  # ---- KDE — ICES 27.7.D --------------------------------------------------
  events_7d_proj <- events_classified_fr %>%
    mutate(year = lubridate::year(start)) %>%
    filter(year %in% study_years, division == "27.7.D",
           !is.na(lon), !is.na(lat)) %>%
    dplyr::select(year, lon, lat) %>%
    st_as_sf(coords = c("lon","lat"), crs = 4326) %>%
    st_transform(crs_proj) %>%
    mutate(x = st_coordinates(.)[,1], y = st_coordinates(.)[,2]) %>%
    st_drop_geometry()

  kde_7d <- map_dfr(study_years, function(yr) {
    pts <- events_7d_proj %>% filter(year == yr)
    if (nrow(pts) < 50) return(NULL)
    ppp_yr <- tryCatch(
      ppp(x = pts$x, y = pts$y, window = window_7d_owin),
      error = function(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(ppp_yr)) return(NULL)
    kde <- density(ppp_yr, sigma = sigma_7d, dimyx = c(200,200), edge = TRUE)
    as.data.frame(kde) %>%
      rename(x=x, y=y, density=value) %>%
      filter(!is.na(density), density > 0) %>%
      mutate(ndensity = density / max(density), year = yr)
  })

  # ---- Grid-cell effort — ICES 27.7.D ------------------------------------
  events_7d_grid <- events_7d_proj %>%
    mutate(
      x_cell  = floor(x / cell_size) * cell_size + cell_size / 2,
      y_cell  = floor(y / cell_size) * cell_size + cell_size / 2,
      cell_id = paste(x_cell, y_cell, sep = "_"))

  cell_effort_7d <- events_7d_grid %>%
    group_by(year, cell_id, x_cell, y_cell) %>%
    summarise(n_events = n(), .groups = "drop")

  # Full grid (including zero-effort cells) for hotspot maps
  x_range <- seq(floor(min(cell_effort_7d$x_cell)/cell_size)*cell_size,
                 ceiling(max(cell_effort_7d$x_cell)/cell_size)*cell_size, by=cell_size)
  y_range <- seq(floor(min(cell_effort_7d$y_cell)/cell_size)*cell_size,
                 ceiling(max(cell_effort_7d$y_cell)/cell_size)*cell_size, by=cell_size)

  full_grid_sf <- expand_grid(year=study_years, x_cell=x_range, y_cell=y_range) %>%
    st_as_sf(coords=c("x_cell","y_cell"), crs=crs_proj, remove=FALSE) %>%
    st_filter(window_7d_proj %>% st_buffer(cell_size/2)) %>%
    st_drop_geometry()

  cell_effort_full <- full_grid_sf %>%
    left_join(cell_effort_7d %>% dplyr::select(year,x_cell,y_cell,n_events),
              by=c("year","x_cell","y_cell")) %>%
    replace_na(list(n_events=0)) %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    mutate(ndensity = n_events / max(n_events)) %>%
    ungroup()

  # ---- Concentration metrics -----------------------------------------------
  concentration_7d <- cell_effort_7d %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    summarise(
      n_cells      = n(),
      total_events = sum(n_events),
      gini         = ineq::Gini(n_events),
      top10_pct    = {
        s     <- sort(n_events, decreasing=TRUE)
        n_top <- max(1L, ceiling(0.10*length(s)))
        sum(s[seq_len(n_top)]) / sum(s) * 100
      },
      .groups = "drop")

  save(land_study, study_window_proj, study_owin,
       world_proj, fao_div_proj,
       bbox_7d_proj, window_7d_proj, window_7d_owin,
       kde_results, kde_7d,
       cell_effort_7d, cell_effort_full, concentration_7d,
       file = spatial_cache)
  msg("GFW spatial: cache saved → ", spatial_cache)
}
```

```{r load-aer-split}
# Cache: cache_aer_split.RData — single object: aer_split
#
# aer_split is the AER Bottom trawl/seine effort disaggregated to gear-code
# level using FDI proportional split keys. It contains one row per
# (year, country_code, vessel_length, sub_reg, gear_code) with columns:
#   gear_code         — OTB, OTT, PTB, SSC, SDN, or "Unsplit"
#   gear_share        — proportion of stratum days assigned to this gear_code
#   totfishdays_split — totfishdays * gear_share (conserved per stratum)
#   split_source      — "FDI direct" | "FDI pooled fallback" | "Unsplit"
#   gear_type         — "Bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB)" | "Seine (SSC/SDN)" | "Unsplit"
#
# Source data: FDI gear-code CSV written by FDI_channel_analysis.R to:
#   fdi_dir/output/fdi_fishingdays_by_country_sizeclass_gearcode_division_year.csv
#
# Cache invalidated when cache_aer.RData is newer or objects are missing.
# To force rebuild: file.remove(aer_split_cache)

fdi_gearcode_csv <- file.path(fdi_dir, "output",
  "fdi_fishingdays_by_country_sizeclass_gearcode_division_year.csv")

aer_split_cache_mtime <- if (file.exists(aer_split_cache))
  file.mtime(aer_split_cache) else as.POSIXct(0)

aer_split_ok <- file.exists(aer_split_cache) &&
  aer_split_cache_mtime > file.mtime(aer_cache) &&
  "aer_split" %in% load(aer_split_cache, envir = new.env())

if (aer_split_ok) {

  msg("AER split: loading from cache (", format(aer_split_cache_mtime, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), ")")
  load(aer_split_cache)

} else {

  msg("AER split: building gear-code disaggregation ...")

  if (!file.exists(fdi_gearcode_csv)) {
    msg("AER split: FDI gear-code CSV not found at:\n  ", fdi_gearcode_csv)
    msg("  Run FDI_channel_analysis.R first to generate it.")
    msg("  aer_split will not be available — Section 4.1.5 figures will be empty.")
    aer_split <- NULL
  } else {

    # ---- 1. FDI gear-code proportions per stratum ---------------------------
    # Country name to ISO3 map (FDI uses full names, AER uses ISO3)
    cty <- c(BELGIUM="BEL", DENMARK="DNK", FRANCE="FRA", GERMANY="DEU",
             IRELAND="IRL", NETHERLANDS="NLD", SWEDEN="SWE",
             "UNITED KINGDOM"="GBR", "EUROPEAN UNION"=NA_character_)

    # Gear codes that belong to the AER "Bottom trawl/seine" category
    bts_gears <- c("Bottom trawl", "Scottish seine", "Danish seine")

    # Primary split key: FDI shares per (year, country, vessel_lc, division, gear_code)
    # Shares are rescaled to sum to 1 within each stratum (handles suppressed rows).
    fdi_key <- read.csv(fdi_gearcode_csv) |>
      filter(division      %in% study_divisions_fdi,
             gear_category %in% bts_gears,
             fishing_days_sum > 0) |>
      mutate(country_code = cty[country]) |>
      filter(!is.na(country_code),
             year >= aer_years_start, year <= aer_years_end) |>          # FDI reliable 2013–2023
      group_by(year, country_code, vessel_lc, division) |>
      mutate(gear_share = fishing_days_sum / sum(fishing_days_sum)) |>
      ungroup() |>
      dplyr::select(year, country_code, vessel_lc, division, gear_code, gear_share)

    # Pooled fallback key: across all countries and years, by vessel_lc only
    # Applied where the primary key has no match (sparse countries, year gaps)
    fallback_key <- fdi_key |>
      group_by(vessel_lc, gear_code) |>
      summarise(days = sum(gear_share), .groups = "drop") |>  # sum shares as proxy weight
      group_by(vessel_lc) |>
      mutate(gear_share = days / sum(days)) |>
      ungroup() |>
      dplyr::select(vessel_lc, gear_code, gear_share)

    # ---- 2. AER base: Bottom trawl/seine, study area, 2013+ -----------------
    aer_bts <- aer_effort_summary |>
      filter(gear_category == "Bottom trawl/seine",
             sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
             year          >= aer_years_start,
             country_code  %in% report_countries_aer) |>
      mutate(division = normalise_division(sub_reg))

    # ---- 3. Primary join ----------------------------------------------------
    aer_joined <- aer_bts |>
      left_join(fdi_key,
                by = c("year", "country_code",
                        "vessel_length" = "vessel_lc", "division"))

    # ---- 4. Apply fallback for unmatched strata (one expand per missing row) -
    aer_good    <- aer_joined |> filter(!is.na(gear_share))
    aer_missing <- aer_joined |>
      filter(is.na(gear_share)) |>
      dplyr::select(-gear_code, -gear_share) |>
      left_join(fallback_key,
                by = c("vessel_length" = "vessel_lc"),
                relationship = "many-to-many") |>
      mutate(gear_share = replace_na(gear_share, 1),
             gear_code  = replace_na(gear_code,  "Unsplit"))

    # ---- 5. Combine, compute split days, label ------------------------------
    aer_split <- bind_rows(
        aer_good |> mutate(split_source = "FDI direct"),
        aer_missing |> mutate(
          split_source = if_else(gear_code == "Unsplit",
                                 "Unsplit", "FDI pooled fallback"))
      ) |>
      mutate(
        totfishdays_split = totfishdays * gear_share,
        gear_type = case_when(
          gear_code %in% c("SSC","SDN")        ~ "Seine (SSC/SDN)",
          gear_code %in% c("OTB","OTT","PTB")  ~ "Bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB)",
          TRUE                                  ~ "Unsplit"
        )
      )

    # ---- 6. Conservation check ----------------------------------------------
    orig  <- aer_bts |>
      distinct(year, country_code, vessel_length, sub_reg, totfishdays) |>
      pull(totfishdays) |> sum(na.rm=TRUE)
    split <- sum(aer_split$totfishdays_split, na.rm=TRUE)
    ratio <- round(split / orig, 4)
    msg("AER split conservation: original=", round(orig),
        "  split=", round(split), "  ratio=", ratio)
    if (abs(ratio - 1) > 0.001)
      warning("Conservation check FAILED (ratio=", ratio, ")")

    save(aer_split, file = aer_split_cache)
    msg("AER split: cache saved → ", aer_split_cache)
  }
}
```

# Executive Summary

Background and aim. The English Channel and southern North Sea (ICES divisions 27.4.c, 27.7.d and 27.7.e) support some of the most intensively exploited fishing grounds in Europe, with important fisheries for France, the United King-dom, Belgium and the Netherlands. Over the past decade these fisheries have been shaped by three concurrent forces: declining fish stocks, post-Brexit access restructuring, and the rapid expansion of offshore wind farms in the southern North Sea. Against this background, this report was commissioned by Cornelis Vrolijk to provide an objective, evidence-based characterisation of fishing effort, landings and spatial distribution in the study area over the period 2008–2023 (AER), 2013–2023 (FDI) and 2013–2025 (GFW), with particular focus on the flyshoot segment in which the company operates.

Approach. Three complementary data sources were integrated: the STECF Annual Economic Report (AER, STECF 25-07), providing official fishing effort and landings by fleet segment; the STECF Fisheries Dependent Information database (FDI, STECF 25-10), used to disaggregate the AER bottom trawl/seine category into conventional otter trawl (OTB) and seine (SSC/SDN) gears; and Global Fishing Watch (GFW) AIS-derived fishing event data, used for spatial analysis of effort distribution and concentration. Kernel density estimation and two concentration metrics, the Gini coefficient and top-10% cell share, were applied to GFW data for ICES 27.7.D to quantify temporal trends in spatial concentration.

Key findings. Total fishing effort in the study area declined by approximately 30% between 2008 and 2023, driven primarily by contraction of French otter trawl and Belgian and Dutch beam trawl fleets. France dominates the effort picture throughout, contributing around 80% of AER fishing days. The Dutch flyshoot fleet, while small in absolute terms, is the dominant seine fleet in the area, with approximately 70% of Dutch bottom trawl/seine days attributable to SSC/SDN gears. Landings are dominated by flatfishes, scallops and shrimps. Flatfish landings declined by more than 60% since 2008, consistent with poor stock status for Channel sole and plaice. Scallop landings increased markedly since 2016, supported by record biomass in the Baie de Seine.

GFW spatial analysis reveals persistent fishing hotspots in the Pas de Calais and the Baie de Seine. Dutch effort in 27.4.C shows progressive spatial compression, likely linked to expanding wind farm footprints. Post-Brexit restructuring is visible from 2021 in the form of declining UK effort in 27.7.e and increasing spatial separation between national fleets. Spatial concentration in 27.7.D increased from a Gini coefficient of around 0.53–0.57 in 2013–2016 to 0.60–0.66 by 2019–2023, with a peak of 50% of total effort concentrated in the top-10% of grid cells in 2020, pointing to a structur-al shift rather than a temporary anomaly.

Conclusions. The fisheries in the Channel and Southern North Sea are undergoing a long-term structural contraction in effort, accompanied by declining landings of key flatfish species and progressive spatial concentration of the remaining fleet into a smaller number of heavily fished areas. The Dutch flyshoot fleet occupies a small but stable position within this system. The combination of AER, FDI and GFW data provides a robust multi-source baseline that can be used to contextualise the position of the Vrolijk fleet within the broader Channel fisheries, and to monitor future changes in fleet composition, spatial distribution and compliance with bilateral management arrangements.

# Nederlandse samenvatting

Achtergrond en doel. Het Engelse Kanaal en de zuidelijke Noordzee (ICES divisies 27.4.c, 27.7.d en 27.7.e) behoren tot de meest intensief beviste wateren van Europa, met belangrijke visserijen voor Frankrijk, het Verenigd Koninkrijk, Bel-gië en Nederland. In het afgelopen decennium zijn deze visserijen beïnvloed door drie gelijktijdige ontwikkelingen: dalende visbestanden, herstructurering van de toegang na Brexit, en de snelle uitbreiding van offshore windparken in de zuidelijke Noordzee. In dit kader werd dit rapport in opdracht van Cornelis Vrolijk opgesteld, met als doel een ob-jectieve, op feiten gebaseerde beschrijving te geven van de visserij-inspanning, aanvoer en ruimtelijke verdeling in het studiegebied over de periode 2008–2023 (AER), 2013–2023 (FDI) en 2013–2025 (GFW), met bijzondere aandacht voor het flyshoot-segment.

Aanpak. Drie complementaire databronnen zijn gecombineerd: het STECF Jaarlijks Economisch Rapport (AER, STECF 25-07) voor officiële visserij-inspanning en aanvoer per vlootsegment; de STECF Fisheries Dependent Information-database (FDI, STECF 25-10) om de AER-categorie “bordenvisserij/zegen” te splitsen in conventionele bordenvisserij (OTB) en flyshoot (SSC/SDN); en Global Fishing Watch (GFW) AIS-gebaseerde visserijdata voor ruimtelijke analyse. Kerneldichtheidsschatting en twee concentratiematen, de Gini-coëfficiënt en het aandeel van de top-10%-cellen, zijn toegepast op GFW-data voor ICES divisie 27.7.D.

Belangrijkste bevindingen. De totale visserij-inspanning in het studiegebied daalde met circa 30% tussen 2008 en 2023, voornamelijk door inkrimping van de Franse bordenvisserij (OTB) en de Belgische en Nederlandse boomkorvis-serij. Frankrijk domineert het gehele inspanningspatroon en levert circa 80% van de AER-visdagen. De Nederlandse flyshoot-vloot is in absolute termen klein, maar is de dominante zegenvisserij in het gebied: circa 70% van de Neder-landse bordenvisserij/zegen-visdagen is toe te schrijven aan zegentuigen (SSC/SDN). De aanvoer wordt gedomineerd door platvis, sint-jakobsschelpen en garnalen. De aanvoer van platvis daalde met meer dan 60% ten opzichte van 2008, consistent met de slechte bestandsstatus van tong en schol in het Kanaal. De aanvoer van sint-jakobsschelpen nam sterk toe na 2016, gesteund door recordbiomassa in de Baie de Seine.

De GFW-ruimtelijke analyse laat persistente visserijhotspots zien in het Nauw van Calais en de Baie de Seine. De Neder-landse inspanning in 27.4.C vertoont een progressieve ruimtelijke compressie, waarschijnlijk gerelateerd aan de uit-breiding van windparkgebieden. De gevolgen van Brexit zijn zichtbaar vanaf 2021: de Britse inspanning in 27.7.e neemt af en de nationale vloten vissen steeds meer in afzonderlijke gebieden. De ruimtelijke concentratie in 27.7.D nam toe van een Gini-coëfficiënt van 0,53–0,57 in 2013–2016 naar 0,60–0,66 in 2019–2023, met een piek waarbij 50% van de totale inspanning was geconcentreerd in 10% van de rastercellen in 2020. Dit lijkt een structurele verschuiving.

Conclusies. De visserij in het kanaal en de zuidelijke Noordzee ondergaat een langdurige structurele krimp in inspan-ning, gepaard met dalende aanvoer van belangrijke platvissoorten en toenemende ruimtelijke concentratie van de resterende vloot. De Nederlandse flyshoot-vloot neemt een kleine maar stabiele positie in binnen dit systeem. De com-binatie van AER-, FDI- en GFW-data biedt een robuuste, meervoudige databasis die kan worden ingezet om de positie van de Vrolijk-vloot te contextualiseren binnen de bredere Channel-visserij, en om toekomstige veranderingen in vloot-samenstelling, ruimtelijke verdeling en naleving van bilaterale beheersafspraken te monitoren.


# 2. Introduction

## 2.1 Background

This study looks into the international fisheries developments in the English Channel and Southern North Sea in the past 15 years. Over this period there has  been an increase in the fisheries for squid and cuttlefish in the Channel and more recently also in the Southern North Sea. This change in fishing patterns has come under increasing public and media scrutiny, including critical coverage in the Netherlands (e.g. Follow the Money). This study attempts to provide a thorough knowledge base on the Channel and Southern North Sea fisheries using data from different sources: 1) STECF Annual Economic Report (AER, STECF 25-03 & 25-07), 2) STECF Fisheries Dependent Information (FDI; STECF, 2025b) and 3) Global Fishing Watch data (https://globalfishingwatch.org). The aim is to provide an objective, evidence-based assessment of the fisheries development in terms of effort and catches of fleets operating in the Channel and the available scientific literature on those fisheries.

The report was commissioned by Cornelis Vrolijk company (https://www.cornelisvrolijk.eu) and executed by Martin Pastoors Fish & Fisheries.  

## 2.2 Objectives

- To quantify trends in fishing effort and landings in the Channel (2008/2013–present) using official STECF statistics (AER), with spatial distribution characterised using GFW AIS data.
- To compile a scientifically grounded overview of the fisheries in the Channel, with particular focus on sustainability, ecosystem effects and the positioning of the flyshoot fishery.

## 2.3 Study area and scope

The study covers ICES divisions 27.4.c (southern North Sea), 27.7.d (eastern English Channel) and 27.7.e (western English Channel). The combination of 27.4c, 27.7.d and 27.7.e will be called "study area" in the report.

The period of analysis is 2008–2023 for effort and landings trends (AER, data for 2024 was not available for France and therefore 2024 has been left out) and 2013–present for spatial analysis (GFW).

# 3. Material & Methods

## 3.1 Literature review approach

The literature review underpinning Sections 4.4 and draws on four categories of sources:

**Scientific literature** was identified through targeted searches of Web of Science, Scopus and Google Scholar using the terms: *English Channel fisheries*, *Channel demersal fisheries*, *flyshoot*, *Danish seine Channel*, *beam trawl North Sea Channel*, *scallop Pecten maximus Channel*, *seabed disturbance trawl*, *AIS fishing effort*, and combinations thereof. Priority was given to peer-reviewed articles published since 2010, supplemented by earlier foundational studies where relevant (e.g. Eigaard et al. 2016; Depestele et al. 2016).

**ICES working group reports** were sourced from the ICES library (https://www.ices.dk), primarily:

- *Working Group on Celtic Seas Ecoregion* (WGCSE, ICES 2025a) — principal source for demersal stocks in the Channel (sole, plaice, whiting, sea bass, monkfish, megrim, mullet) and for the broader ecosystem and fisheries context of 27.7.d/e.
- *Working Group on the Assessment of Demersal Stocks in the North Sea and Skagerrak* (WGNSSK, ICES 2025c) — consulted for stocks with distributions spanning both 27.4.c and the Channel (e.g. plaice, dab, horse mackerel).
- *Working Group on Widely Distributed Stocks* (WGWIDE, ICES 2025e) — responsible for the assessment of mackerel (*Scomber scombrus*) and horse mackerel (*Trachurus trachurus* western stock), both of which can be important bycatch species in the study area.
- *Working Group on Cephalopod Fisheries and Life History* (WGCEPH, ICES 2025d) — consulted for cuttlefish (*Sepia officinalis*) and squid (*Loligo* spp., *Illex* spp.) in the Channel and North Sea. WGCEPH does not produce formal TAC advice but provides the best available science on stock status and drivers of variability.

ICES advice sheets for the relevant stocks were also consulted directly.

**Official statistics and national sources** include the STECF AER (primary quantitative source for this report), Ifremer fleet and stock assessment reports, the UK Marine Management Organisation (MMO) annual sea fisheries statistics, and the Belgian ILVO annual fleet reports. Where possible, the most recent published edition was used.

**Policy and grey literature** includes EU regulation texts, the UK–EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement fisheries annex and parliamentary reports on post-Brexit fisheries.

All quantitative claims made in the literature sections are cross-referenced with the AER and GFW results presented in Section 4, and discrepancies or gaps are noted where they arise.

## 3.2 STECF AER data (effort and landings trends)

The Annual Economic Report (AER) data were obtained from the STECF 25-07 data release (*EU Fleet Economic and Transversal data, fleet segment level*). The AER provides fishing effort (fishing days, sea days, kW-days, GT-days) and landed weight and value by fleet segment (country × fishing technique × vessel length class), disaggregated by FAO division. 

The AER analyses in this report cover the period **2008–2023**. The end year of 2023 reflects the absence of French effort and landings data for 2024 in the current STECF 25-07 release. Unfortunately, the UK could not be included in the AER analyses because no data are available for the UK in the STECF series following Brexit. The AER data does not distinguish between bottom trawl and seine fisheries; they are reported as a combined category. 

### 3.2.1 Vessel length classes

The AER reports effort and landings by vessel length class (VLC), defined by overall length (LOA) in metres. Six standard classes are used throughout this report, as defined in the STECF fleet data collection framework:

```{r vlc-table, echo=FALSE}
tibble::tibble(
  `Code`              = c("VL0010","VL1012","VL1218","VL1824","VL2440","VL40XX"),
  `Length range (m)`  = c("< 10","10–12","12–18","18–24","24–40","> 40"),
  `Typical vessel type` = c(
    "Small inshore vessels (outboard/inboard motor)",
    "Small coastal vessels",
    "Medium coastal/demersal vessels",
    "Medium offshore vessels, beam trawlers, flyshoot",
    "Large demersal and pelagic trawlers",
    "Freezer trawlers"
  )
) |>
  flextable::flextable() |>
  style_ft(font_size = 9) |>
  flextable::set_caption(
    caption = tab_nums("vlc_table",
      "Vessel length classes (VLC) used in STECF AER data and throughout this report.")
  )
```

VL0010 and VL40XX are included in data tables but excluded from some effort figures where their small contribution makes them difficult to display alongside the dominant VL1218–VL2440 classes. All classes are included in the Annex D tables.

### 3.2.2 Species groups

Landings in the AER are reported at the individual species level using FAO 3-alpha species codes. For summary figures and tables, individual species are aggregated into ecologically and commercially meaningful species groups. The grouping was applied using FAO 3-alpha codes as the primary key (reliable and consistent across member states) with species name pattern matching as a fallback. Table `r tab_nums("spp_group_table", display="cite")` lists the species groups used and the main constituent species.

```{r spp-group-table, echo=FALSE}

## 3.3 STECF FDI data — limitations and use as gear-splitting key

The STECF Fisheries Dependent Information (FDI) dataset was obtained for the study area and period. Unfortunately the FDI Landings table is EU-aggregated (no country breakdown) and the Effort and Catches tables suffer from substantial confidentiality suppression in many strata. In addition, the spatial FDI tables were not available on the STECF website at the time of analysis. Therefore, the FDI data has not been used as the main source of the data for the report. 

Despite these limitations, the FDI Effort table retains one piece of information not available in the AER data: **gear code at the FAO level** (e.g. OTB, OTT, SSC, SDN, PTB). The AER combines all of these into a single `Bottom trawl/seine` category, which conflates conventional otter trawl (OTB) with Danish/Scottish seine (SSC/SDN),two gears with very different fishing patterns and fleet compositions. The FDI gear-code information is therefore used to disaggregate the AER `Bottom trawl/seine` category, as described below.

**Splitting approach.** For each stratum `(year, country, vessel length class, division)`, the share of each gear code within the `Bottom trawl/seine` total was computed from the FDI Effort table. This proportional split key was then applied to the corresponding AER fishing days, so that the total days in each stratum are conserved exactly. Shares in the FDI strata are rescaled to sum to 1 within each stratum, handling any within-stratum confidentiality suppression transparently.

**Coverage and fallback rules.** FDI data are used for 2013–2023 only. Post-2013 strata with no FDI coverage (primarily IRL, DNK, and some BEL and DEU strata where FDI reported zero or suppressed days) are assigned a pooled fallback split key derived from the FDI data aggregated across all available years and countries, stratified by vessel length class.

**Limitations.** Countries for which FDI coverage is sparse (IRL, DNK, DEU) receive a pooled fleet-average split that may not reflect their actual gear mix. Results for these countries should be interpreted with caution and are excluded from the figures showing the French and Dutch trends.

## 3.4 GFW data (spatial effort distribution and concentration)

Fishing activity data were retrieved via the Global Fishing Watch (GFW) API (`gfwr` v3.0) using the Events endpoint. Vessel metadata (country, gear type, gross tonnage) were obtained from the GFW vessel registry (https://globalfishingwatch.org, Kroodsma et al, 2018).

Recent publication have shown that the haul based effort from GFW may not be a reliable indicator for fishing effort for trawl based gears (Hintzen et al 2025). Therefore, we define GFW days at sea in this report as vessel-days: for each day, each vessel is assigned to the ICES division in which it spent the majority of its time, based on the spatial distribution of AIS positions recorded during that day. This definition is therefore a simple presence-day metric. The effort trends derived from GFW data were found to be very different from effort trends in AER (and FDI) data. An important limitation of the GFW data is that vessels below the AIS carriage requirement threshold (typically 15 m LOA, though requirements vary by country and fishing area) are systematically under-represented or absent. This means that gears dominated by small inshore vessels — gillnets, pots and traps, handlines — are structurally under-counted relative to larger trawl and seine vessels, which carry AIS as a mandatory requirement. Therefore, the GFW data are used exclusively used for the spatial analysis using effort density maps, spatial hotspots, and effort concentration metrics. The GFW spatial analysis covers the full period 2013–2025.

Kernel density estimation of spatial effort distribution

The spatial distribution of fishing effort was characterised using kernel density estimation (KDE), a standard non-parametric method for converting a set of discrete point locations into a smooth continuous surface representing effort intensity (Silverman, 1986). For each year, fishing event coordinates were projected into a metric coordinate system (UTM Zone 30N) and a Gaussian kernel with bandwidth σ = 20 km was applied across the full study area, and σ = 10 km for the focused analysis of ICES 27.7.D. The narrower bandwidth for 27.7.D resolves finer-scale spatial structure within the eastern Channel. Both bandwidths are fixed across years so that changes in the density surface reflect genuine shifts in fishing distribution rather than smoothing artefacts. Land is excluded from the estimation window. The resulting surface is normalised to a 0–1 scale within each year, making spatial patterns directly comparable across years regardless of differences in total effort; for absolute effort levels, the AER-based effort figures in Section 4.2 should be consulted alongside the KDE maps. KDE is widely used in fisheries spatial analysis to identify persistent hotspots, characterise seasonal grounds and detect shifts in fleet distribution over time (Gerritsen & Lordan, 2011; Kroodsma et al., 2018).

Spatial concentration metrics: Gini coefficient and top-10% cell share

Two complementary metrics were computed annually for ICES 27.7.D on a regular 5 km × 5 km grid to quantify how concentrated fishing effort is in space, rather than simply where it occurs. The Gini coefficient is a well-established inequality measure — originally from economics and widely applied in fisheries spatial analysis (Greenstreet et al., 2009; Eigaard et al., 2017) — that summarises the full distribution of effort across all grid cells on a scale from 0 (effort perfectly uniform across all cells) to 1 (all effort in a single cell). Values above approximately 0.7 indicate strong spatial concentration; a rising Gini over time signals progressive compression of effort into fewer areas, which may reflect displacement from previously accessible grounds, regulatory closures or increasing targeting efficiency. The top-10% cell share is a more intuitive companion metric: it expresses what percentage of total annual fishing events falls within the 10% of grid cells that were most intensively fished that year. If effort were uniform this would equal 10%; values of 40–70% are typical in concentrated demersal fisheries. Together the two metrics capture different aspects of concentration — the Gini reflects the shape of the full distribution while the top-10% share highlights the intensity of the most-fished areas — and tracking both annually allows changes in spatial footprint to be detected even when total effort remains stable.

## 3.5 Literature review approach

The literature review underpinning Sections 4.1 and 4.8 draws on four categories of sources:

**Scientific literature** was identified through targeted searches of Web of Science, Scopus and Google Scholar using the terms: *English Channel fisheries*, *Channel demersal fisheries*, *flyshoot*, *Danish seine Channel*, *beam trawl North Sea Channel*, *scallop Pecten maximus Channel*, *seabed disturbance trawl*, *AIS fishing effort*, and combinations thereof. Priority was given to peer-reviewed articles published since 2010, supplemented by earlier foundational studies where relevant (e.g. Eigaard et al. 2016; Depestele et al. 2016).

**ICES working group reports** were sourced from the ICES library (https://www.ices.dk), primarily:

- *Working Group on Celtic Seas Ecoregion* (WGCSE, ICES 2025a) — principal source for demersal stocks in the Channel (sole, plaice, whiting, sea bass, monkfish, megrim, mullet) and for the broader ecosystem and fisheries context of 27.7.d/e.
- *Working Group on the Assessment of Demersal Stocks in the North Sea and Skagerrak* (WGNSSK, ICES 2024c) — consulted for stocks with distributions spanning both 27.4.c and the Channel (e.g. plaice, dab, horse mackerel).
- *Working Group on Widely Distributed Stocks* (WGWIDE, ICES 2024e) — responsible for the assessment of mackerel (*Scomber scombrus*) and horse mackerel (*Trachurus trachurus* western stock), both of which can be important bycatch species in the study area.
- *Working Group on Cephalopod Fisheries and Life History* (WGCEPH, ICES 2024d) — consulted for cuttlefish (*Sepia officinalis*) and squid (*Loligo* spp., *Illex* spp.) in the Channel and North Sea. WGCEPH does not produce formal TAC advice but provides the best available science on stock status and drivers of variability.
- *Working Group on Ecosystem Effects of Fishing Activities* (WGECO) — for seabed disturbance and ecosystem-level assessments.

ICES advice sheets for the relevant stocks were also consulted directly.

**Official statistics and national sources** include the STECF AER (primary quantitative source for this report), Ifremer fleet and stock assessment reports, the UK Marine Management Organisation (MMO) annual sea fisheries statistics, and the Belgian ILVO annual fleet reports. Where possible, the most recent published edition was used.

**Policy and grey literature** includes EU regulation texts, the UK–EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement fisheries annex, and parliamentary reports on post-Brexit fisheries.

All quantitative claims made in the literature sections are cross-referenced with the AER and GFW results presented in Section 4, and discrepancies or gaps are noted where they arise.


# 4. Results

## 4.1 Landings trends — STECF AER

### 4.1.1 landings by species during 2008-2023

The overall landings by species in the study area (27.4.c, 27.7.d and 27.7.e) during all of the years available in the AER data are shown in the figure below (left: all gears, right: bottom trawl/seine, beam trawl and dredge). Herring, scallops and tangle (seaweed) have the highest landings for all gears. For the selected demersal fisheries in the study area, scallops, shrimp and plaice have the highest landings overall. 

```{r aer-landings-top-species, fig.height=6, fig.cap=fig_nums("landings_top20")}
p1 <- aer_landings_summary |>
  filter(country_code %in% report_countries_aer,
         sub_reg      %in% study_divisions_aer) |>
  group_by(species_code, species_name) |>
  summarise(total_t=sum(live_weight_t, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  slice_max(total_t, n=20) |>
  mutate(species_label = paste0(species_name," (",species_code,")"),
         species_label = fct_reorder(species_label, total_t)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x=total_t/1000, y=species_label)) +
  geom_col(fill="#4E79A7") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,NA), expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0.03))) +
  labs(subtitle = "All gears",
       x="Total landed weight (1000 t)", y="") +
  theme_bw()

p2 <- aer_landings_summary |>
  filter(country_code %in% report_countries_aer,
         sub_reg      %in% study_divisions_aer,
         gear_category %in% capacity_gears) |>
  group_by(species_code, species_name) |>
  summarise(total_t=sum(live_weight_t, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  slice_max(total_t, n=20) |>
  mutate(species_label = paste0(species_name," (",species_code,")"),
         species_label = fct_reorder(species_label, total_t)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x=total_t/1000, y=species_label)) +
  geom_col(fill="#4E79A7") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits=c(0,NA), expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0.03))) +
  labs(subtitle = "Selected gears",
       x="Total landed weight (1000 t)", y="") +
  theme_bw()

p1 + p2 +
  plot_annotation(
    title   = paste0("AER — Top 20 species by total landed weight  |  ",
                     "Divisions: ", paste(study_divisions_aer, collapse=" & ")),
    caption = paste0("Total landed weight per species, ",
                     aer_years_start, "–", aer_years_end,
                     ". Left: all gears. Right: selected gears only."),
    theme   = theme(
      plot.title   = element_text(size=12, face="bold"),
      plot.caption = element_text(size=8,  colour="grey40")
    )
  )
```

Tangle (LQD) is a seaweed species being harvested from the sea (*Laminaria digitata*). Common European bittersweet (GKL) is a shellfish species (*Glycymeris glycymeris*).


### 4.1.2 Total landed weight by year, country and gear

Total landings by gear and country are shown in the figure below. Highest landings are in the category Other/mixed which includes pelagic trawl (for e.g. herring). Beam trawl, bottom trawl/seine and dredge are the three gear types that generate somewhat comparable amounts of landings. Beam trawl is dominated by the Netherlands and bottom trawl/seine and dredge by France. 

```{r aer-landings-total, fig.height=8, fig.cap=fig_nums("landings_gear")}
aer_landings_summary |>
  remove_pelagic_anomaly() |>
  filter(country_code %in% report_countries_aer,
         sub_reg      %in% study_divisions_aer) |>
  group_by(year, country_code, gear_category) |>
  summarise(live_weight_t=sum(live_weight_t, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  complete(year, country_code, gear_category, fill=list(live_weight_t=NA_real_)) |>
  mutate(country_code = factor(country_code, levels=report_countries_aer)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x=year, y=live_weight_t, colour=country_code)) +
  geom_line(na.rm=TRUE) + geom_point(size=1.5, na.rm=TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values=flag_colours, drop=FALSE, na.value="grey70",
                      name="Country") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(aer_years_start, aer_years_end, by=2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,NA), expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0.05))) +
  facet_wrap(~gear_category) +
  labs(title   = "AER — Landed weight by gear category",
       subtitle = paste("Divisions:", paste(study_divisions_aer, collapse=" & ")),
       caption  = pelagic_anomaly_note,
       x="Year", y="Landed weight (t)") +

  theme(strip.text   = element_text(size=7),
        axis.text.x  = element_text(angle=45, hjust=1),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        plot.caption = element_text(size=6.5, colour="grey40"))
```


### 4.1.3 Total landed weight for Other/mixed gear by year, country and species group

The `Other/mixed` gear category covers a highly diverse range of fishing techniques and target species that do not fit neatly into the main AER gear categories. The composition of this category differs markedly by country. French `Other/mixed` landings are dominated by seaweeds (tangle LQD and kelp LAH, harvested mechanically from the seabed) and pelagic fish (herring, mackerel, sardine and horse mackerel), together accounting for over 60% of French `Other/mixed` volume throughout the series. The increase in French `Other/mixed` landings since 2019 — visible in the preceding landings-by-gear figure — is driven largely by growing seaweed harvests rather than increasing pelagic or demersal fishing activity. Dutch `Other/mixed` landings are almost entirely pelagic fish, consistent with the Dutch pelagic trawl fleet (pair trawlers targeting herring, horse mackerel and mackerel in the Channel), though showing considerable interannual variability linked to stock availability and quota allocation. German `Other/mixed` landings are a modest but stable contribution, also predominantly pelagic. Belgian `Other/mixed` landings are negligible at this scale and have been omitted

```{r aer-landings-species-country-groups, fig.height=5, fig.cap=fig_nums("landings_spp_grp_cty")}
plot_data <- aer_landings_summary |>
  remove_pelagic_anomaly() |>
  filter(sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
         gear_category == "Other/mixed",
         country_code  %in% report_countries_aer,
         country_code != "BEL",
         year          %in% aer_years_start:aer_years_end) |>
  mutate(species_group = assign_species_group(species_code, species_name),
         species_group = if_else(is.na(species_group), "Other", species_group),
         species_group = factor(species_group,
                                levels = c(species_group_levels, "Other"))) |>
  group_by(year, country_code, species_group) |>
  summarise(live_weight_t = sum(live_weight_t, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  complete(year         = aer_years_start:aer_years_end,
           # country_code = report_countries_aer,
           species_group,
           fill = list(live_weight_t = 0)) |>
  # Set 2012 NLD to NA so the bar is fully absent
  mutate(live_weight_t = if_else(
    country_code == "NLD" & year == 2012,
    NA_real_, live_weight_t)) |>
  mutate(country_code = factor(country_code, levels=report_countries_aer))

asterisk_data <- data.frame(
  country_code = factor("NLD", levels=report_countries_aer),

)

ggplot(plot_data, aes(x=year, y=live_weight_t/1000, fill=species_group)) +

       caption  = pelagic_anomaly_note,

        legend.position = "bottom",

### 4.1.4 Key species groups — landings by country

Landings in the study area are dominated by flatfishes, scallops and shrimps in terms of volume, with flatfish landings showing a marked decline from around 40,000 t in 2008 to below 15,000 t by 2023, driven almost entirely by the Dutch (NLD) and Belgian (BEL) fleets. This is consistent with the contraction of beam trawl effort over this period. Scallop landings are dominated by France (FRA) and show an increasing trend since 2016, reaching record levels in 2022–2023. Shrimp landings are predominantly Dutch, in the Southern North Sea and relatively stable. Cephalopod landings (cuttlefish and squid) are France-dominated and show moderate interannual variability. Landings of mackerel, horse mackerel, whiting, mullets and gurnards are comparatively low across all countries.

```{r aer-landings-species-country, fig.height=10, fig.cap=fig_nums("landings_spp_cty")}

Mullets, mackerel and horse mackerel show negligible landings across all gears.

## 4.2 Effort trends (STECF AER)

### 4.2.1 Total fishing days by year and country (all gears)

Total fishing effort in the study area declined from around 235,000 days in 2008 to approximately 160,000 days in 2023, a reduction of roughly 30% over the period. France consistently dominates total effort, accounting for approximately 80% of fishing days throughout the series. The Netherlands is the second largest contributor, with effort relatively stable over the period. Belgian and German effort is small and declining. The overall downward trend is driven primarily by reductions in French effort, with a notable step-down around 2019–2020 that may partly reflect COVID-19 disruption as well as post-Brexit access restrictions in subsequent years.

### 4.2.2 Total fishing days by year, country and gear category

The breakdown of effort by gear category reveals that the dominant gears in the study area are bottom trawl/seine, dredge, gillnet and pot/trap, with the `Other/mixed` category contributing a substantial and growing share in 27.7.D (see Section 4.2.6 for further analysis of that category). Bottom trawl/seine effort is predominantly French throughout, with a gradual declining trend. Dredge effort is almost exclusively French, reflecting the scallop fleet operating in 27.7.D and 27.7.E. The Dutch fleet is most visible in beam trawl and, to a lesser extent, `Other/mixed`. Belgian effort appears primarily in beam trawl and shows the strongest decline of any national fleet over the period.

```{r aer-effort-gear-cat, fig.height=8, fig.cap=fig_nums("effort_gear_cat")}

### 4.2.3 Total fishing days by year, country and vessel length class

Fishing effort by vessel length class reveals distinct fleet structures by country. The French fleet (FRA) dominates across the smaller vessel size classes, with the largest absolute number of fishing days in the smaller vessel classes (VL0010–VL1218). This reflects the broad size distribution of the French demersal fleet. French effort shows a gradual declining trend across most size classes over the period. The Dutch fleet (NLD) is concentrated in the medium-to-large vessel classes (VL1824 and VL40XX), consistent with the flyshoot and beam trawl fleet composition, and shows relatively stable effort over time. Belgian effort (BEL) is most visible in the VL1824 class and shows a clear declining trend, consistent with the contraction of the Belgian beam trawl fleet documented in the landings data. German effort (DEU) is negligible across all size classes. Notably, the VL1824 class shows the most multi-country competition for effort, with French, Dutch and Belgian vessels all active in this size range.

```{r aer-effort-trend, fig.height=6, fig.cap=fig_nums("effort_gear")}
aer_effort_summary |>

         gear_category %in% capacity_gears) |>
  group_by(year, country_code, vessel_length) |>
  summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  complete(year, country_code, vessel_length, fill=list(totfishdays=NA_real_)) |>
  mutate(country_code  = factor(country_code,  levels=report_countries_aer),
         vessel_length = factor(vessel_length,
                                levels=c("VL0010","VL1012","VL1218",
                                         "VL1824","VL2440","VL40XX"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(x=year, y=totfishdays, colour=country_code)) +
  geom_line(na.rm=TRUE) + geom_point(size=1.5, na.rm=TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values=flag_colours, drop=FALSE, na.value="grey70",
                      name="Country") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(aer_years_start, aer_years_end, by=2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,NA), expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0.05))) +
  facet_wrap(~vessel_length, ncol=3) +
  labs(title    = "AER: Fishing days by vessel length class",
       subtitle = paste0("Divisions: ", paste(study_divisions_aer, collapse=" & "),
                         "  —  Gears: ", paste(capacity_gears, collapse=", ")),
       x="Year", y="Fishing days", colour="Country") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(strip.text=element_text(size=8), axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1),
        legend.position="bottom")
```

### 4.2.4 Total fishing days by year and vessel size class (selected gears)

Total effort for selected gears declined from around 120,000 days in 2008 to approximately 75,000 days in 2023. The decline is most pronounced in the medium vessel classes (VL1218 and VL1824), which together historically dominated total effort. Smaller vessels (VL0010–VL1012) show greater stability, while the largest vessels (VL2440–VL40XX) contribute relatively little throughout.

        legend.position="right")
```

### 4.2.5 Fishing days by year, country, gear and vessel size

The figure below reveals clear fleet specialisation by gear and vessel size. French vessels dominate bottom trawl/seine effort across all size classes, with a modest declining trend. Dutch effort is concentrated in beam trawl (VL1824 and VL40XX) and shows the strongest decline over the period, consistent with the contraction of the Dutch beam trawl fleet. Belgian effort is similarly concentrated in beam trawl VL1824, also declining markedly. Dredge effort is almost exclusively French across small-to-medium vessel classes (VL1012–VL1218), and relatively stable.

```{r aer-effort-gt, fig.height=10, fig.cap=fig_nums("effort_gt")}
# exclude_vlc <- c("VL0010","VL40XX","UNKNOWN","NK")
exclude_vlc <- c("UNKNOWN","NK")

aer_effort_raw |>

### 4.2.6 Disaggregation of bottom trawl/seine into OTB and SSC/SDN (FDI-derived)

As described in Section 3.3, the AER Bottom trawl/seine category was disaggregated into conventional otter trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB) and seine (SSC/SDN) gears using proportional split keys derived from the STECF FDI Effort data. The left panel shows that the category is heavily dominated by conventional bottom trawl throughout 2013–2023, with overall fishing days declining by over 30% over the period. The right panel shows the gear-type share based on direct FDI splits only: conventional otter trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB) accounts for approximately 85–90% of days, with seine (SSC/SDN) contributing 10–15% and showing a modest upward trend in its share towards the end of the period. The picture varies strongly by country: France is almost exclusively OTB (~96%), while the Netherlands is predominantly seine (SSC/SDN, ~70%), reflecting the Dutch flyshoot fleet composition. Note that BEL and DEU received pooled fallback splits due to sparse FDI coverage and are therefore excluded from the percentage panel.


```{r aer-split-trend, fig.height=5, fig.width=10, fig.cap=fig_nums("split_total")}
if (!is.null(aer_split)) {

  split_2colours <- c(
    "Bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB)" = "#E15759",
    "Seine (SSC/SDN)"             = "#4E79A7"
  )
  
  p_abs <- aer_split |>
    filter(year <= aer_years_end,
           gear_type != "Unsplit") |>
    group_by(year, gear_type) |>
    summarise(fishdays = sum(totfishdays_split, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
    mutate(gear_type = factor(gear_type, levels=names(split_2colours))) |>
    ggplot(aes(x=year, y=fishdays, fill=gear_type)) +
    geom_col(position="stack", width=0.8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values=split_2colours, name=NULL, guide  = guide_legend(nrow=1)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(aer_split_years_start, aer_years_end, by=2)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,NA), expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0.05)),
                       labels=scales::label_comma()) +
    labs(subtitle="Absolute fishing days", x="Year", y="Fishing days") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(axis.text.x   = element_text(angle=45, hjust=1),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(size=9, colour="grey30"))

p_pct <- aer_split |>
    filter(year         %in% aer_split_years_start:aer_years_end,
           split_source == "FDI direct",
           gear_type    != "Unsplit") |>
    group_by(year, gear_type) |>
    summarise(totdays = sum(totfishdays_split, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
    group_by(year) |>
    mutate(pct = round(100 * totdays / sum(totdays), 0)) |>
    ungroup() |>
    mutate(gear_type = factor(gear_type, levels=names(split_2colours))) |>
    ggplot(aes(x=year, y=pct, colour=gear_type, group=gear_type)) +
    geom_line(linewidth=1) +
    geom_point(size=3) +
    geom_text(aes(label=paste0(pct, "%")),
              vjust=-0.8, size=2.8, show.legend=FALSE) +
    scale_colour_manual(values=split_2colours, name=NULL) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks=seq(aer_split_years_start, aer_years_end, by=2)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0, 100),
                       expand=expansion(mult=c(0, 0.08)),
                       labels=scales::label_percent(scale=1)) +
    labs(subtitle="Gear share (%) — FDI direct splits only",
         x="Year", y="Share of fishing days (%)") +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "none",          # suppress p_pct legend entirely
          axis.text.x     = element_text(angle=45, hjust=1),
          plot.subtitle   = element_text(size=9, colour="grey30"))

p_abs + p_pct +
  plot_layout(guides="collect") +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = "AER — Bottom trawl/seine disaggregated by gear code",
    subtitle = paste0("Divisions: ", paste(study_divisions_aer, collapse=" & "),
                      "  —  FDI gear-code split applied to AER fishing days"),
    theme    = theme(
      plot.title    = element_text(size=11, face="bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size=9, colour="grey30"),
      legend.position = "bottom"    # set here on the annotation theme, not with &
    )
  )

} else {
  cat("aer_split not available.\n")
}
```

## 4.3 Global Fishing Watch (GFW) effort data and comparison with AER

### 4.3.1 Total GFW fishing days by year and country

GFW-derived fishing effort in the study area shows a clear increasing trend from around 53,000 days in 2013 to approximately 90,000 days in 2024–2025, contrasting with the declining trend seen in the AER data. Unlike the AER-based figures, the GFW series includes the United Kingdom (GBR), which accounts for approximately 25–30% of total effort in the area and is the second largest contributor after the Netherlands. The size class breakdown shows that effort is dominated by small vessels (S1 <100 GT), with a growing contribution from this class driving much of the overall increase. French and Dutch effort appears relatively stable in the GFW series, suggesting the overall increase may partly reflect improving AIS coverage over time rather than a genuine increase in fishing activity.

```{r gfw-plot-flag-total, fig.cap=fig_nums("gfw_flag_total")}

y_scale  <- scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, NA),

ax_theme <- theme_bw() +
