### 4.3.2 AER vs GFW effort comparison

The two data sources measure effort differently: AER reports administrative fishing days declared by member states; GFW estimates fishing days from AIS vessel-tracking. The comparison below shows total fishing days over the overlapping period 2013–2023. Note that the AER series excludes GBR (post-Brexit data are not consistently included in the STECF AER) while the GFW series includes all five countries.

Several factors can explain systematic differences between the two series:

- **Method for counting fishing days**: AER records one fishing day as any day on which a vessel is registered as fishing by its country; GFW counts a vessel-day as active when AIS-derived speed and movement patterns are classified as fishing behaviour. The two methods can disagree for the same vessel on the same day.
- **AIS coverage and adoption**: AIS was gradually mandated across the EU fleet between 2008 and 2014. Early years of the GFW series therefore under-represent vessels that did not yet carry AIS transponders, leading to lower GFW effort estimates before ~2014.
- **Small coastal vessels**: Vessels below ~15 m LOA are not required to carry AIS in many jurisdictions. This segment is captured in the AER (via logbook reporting) but largely absent from GFW, causing a structural undercount in GFW relative to AER for gears dominated by small vessels (e.g. pot/trap, gillnet).
- **Gear type assignment**: GFW classifies gear from AIS movement patterns; misclassification can shift effort between gear categories when comparing with AER gear-specific totals.
- **Spatial attribution**: AER effort is attributed to the ICES division declared in the logbook; GFW effort is attributed to the GPS position of the fishing event. In boundary areas the two can differ.

```{r aer-gfw-comparison, fig.height=5, fig.cap=fig_nums("aer_gfw_compare")}
# AER: DEU+NLD+BEL+FRA only (GBR excluded — incomplete in AER post-Brexit)
aer_countries_comparison <- c("DEU","NLD","BEL","FRA")
aer_label <- paste0("AER (", paste(aer_countries_comparison, collapse="+"), ")")
gfw_label <- paste0("GFW (", paste(report_countries_gfw, collapse="+"), ")")

aer_total <- aer_effort_summary |>
  filter(country_code %in% aer_countries_comparison,
         sub_reg      %in% study_divisions_aer,
         year %in% intersect(study_years, seq(aer_years_start, 2023))) |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarise(fishing_days=sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  mutate(source=aer_label)

gfw_total <- fishing_days_study %>%
  filter(vessel_flag %in% report_countries_gfw,
         year %in% intersect(study_years, seq(gfw_years_start, 2023))) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(fishing_days=sum(fishing_days), .groups="drop") %>%
  mutate(source=gfw_label)

bind_rows(aer_total, gfw_total) |>
  ggplot(aes(x=year, y=fishing_days/1000, colour=source, shape=source)) +
  geom_line(linewidth=1) + geom_point(size=2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=study_years) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,NA), expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0.05))) +
  scale_colour_manual(values=setNames(c("#E15759","#4E79A7"), c(aer_label, gfw_label))) +
  scale_shape_manual(values=setNames(c(16L, 17L), c(aer_label, gfw_label))) +
  labs(title    = "Effort comparison: AER vs GFW",
       subtitle = paste0("Divisions: ", paste(study_divisions_aer, collapse=" & ")),
       x="Year", y="Fishing days (1000)", colour="Source", shape="Source") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=45, hjust=1), legend.position="bottom")
```

### 4.3.3 Spatial distribution of GFW fishing events

The spatial distribution of GFW fishing events reveals clear national zoning patterns across the study area. Dutch (NLD) effort is heavily concentrated in the southern North Sea (27.4.C), particularly around and between the wind farm development zones. French (FRA) effort dominates the eastern and western Channel (27.7.D/E), spread broadly across the division. UK (GBR) effort is distributed throughout the Channel, with particular concentration in 27.7.E. The wind farm areas in 27.4.C appear to constrain fishing to the corridors between developments, potentially contributing to spatial concentration of effort in that division.

```{r gfw-plot-spatial-all, fig.height=6, fig.cap=fig_nums("gfw_events_all")}
sample_size <- 20000
events_sample <- events_classified_fr %>%
  dplyr::select(-any_of(c("vessel_flag","vessel_name"))) %>%
  left_join(vessel_meta %>% dplyr::select(vesselId, vessel_flag), by="vesselId") %>%
  mutate(vessel_flag = if_else(vessel_flag %in% report_countries_gfw,
                               vessel_flag, "Other"),
         vessel_flag = factor(vessel_flag,
                               levels=c(report_countries_gfw, "Other"))) %>%
  slice_sample(n=sample_size) %>%
  st_as_sf(coords=c("lon","lat"), crs=4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs_proj) %>%
  mutate(x=st_coordinates(.)[,1], y=st_coordinates(.)[,2]) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  mutate(year = year(start))

ggplot() +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_point(data=events_sample,
             aes(x=x, y=y, colour=vessel_flag),
             size=0.4, alpha=0.7) +
  geom_sf(data=world_proj, fill="grey85", colour="grey50", linewidth=0.3) +
  geom_sf(data=fao_div_proj, fill=NA, colour="black", linewidth=0.5) +
  geom_sf_label(data=fao_div_proj,
                aes(label=division), size=2.5, colour="black",
                fill=alpha("white", 0.6), label.size=0) +
  geom_sf(data = wind_proj %>% filter(STATUS %in% c("Approved","Production")), 
          fill=NA, colour = "grey30", 
        alpha = 0.85, linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_sf(data = wind_proj %>% filter(STATUS %in% c("Planned")), 
          fill=NA, colour = "grey30", linetype = "dashed",
        alpha = 0.85, linewidth = 0.3) +

  scale_colour_manual(values=c(flag_colours, Other="#BAB0AC"),
                      drop=FALSE, na.value="grey70", name="Flag") +
  coord_sf(crs=crs_proj,
           xlim=st_bbox(study_window_proj)[c("xmin","xmax")],
           ylim=st_bbox(study_window_proj)[c("ymin","ymax")],
           expand=TRUE) +
  guides(colour=guide_legend(override.aes=list(size=3, alpha=1))) +
  theme(axis.text=element_blank(), axis.ticks=element_blank(),
        axis.title=element_blank(), legend.position="bottom") +
  labs(title=paste0("GFW fishing events: ", min(events_sample$year),"-", max(events_sample$year)," (sample of ", sample_size, ")"),
       subtitle="ICES 27.4.C / 27.7.D / 27.7.E,  Internal waters excluded",
       caption="Grey solid areas: windfarms operational or approved, dashed areas: planned")
```

### 4.5.2 Spatial distribution of fishing events by year

The annual maps reveal several notable patterns. Dutch (NLD) effort in 27.4.C shows progressive spatial compression over time, likely reflecting the expanding wind farm footprint pushing vessels into narrower corridors. French (FRA) effort in the Channel remains broadly stable in distribution throughout the series. UK (GBR) effort in 27.7.E appears to decline noticeably after 2020, consistent with post-Brexit fleet restructuring. From 2021 onwards, the spatial separation between national fleets becomes more pronounced, suggesting reduced overlap in fishing grounds following the EU-UK TCA access arrangements.

```{r gfw-plot-spatial-by-year, fig.height=10, fig.cap=fig_nums("gfw_events_year")}

events_sample_yr <- events_classified_fr %>%

  filter(year >= gfw_years_start) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  slice_sample(n=sample_size_yr) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  st_as_sf(coords=c("lon","lat"), crs=4326) %>%
  st_transform(crs_proj) %>%
  mutate(x=st_coordinates(.)[,1], y=st_coordinates(.)[,2]) %>%
  st_drop_geometry()

ggplot() +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_point(data=events_sample_yr,
             aes(x=x, y=y, colour=vessel_flag),
             size=0.3, alpha=0.7) +
  geom_sf(data=world_proj, fill="grey85", colour="grey50", linewidth=0.3) +
  geom_sf(data=fao_div_proj, fill=NA, colour="black", linewidth=0.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values=c(flag_colours, Other="#BAB0AC"),
                      drop=FALSE, na.value="grey70", name="Flag") +
  coord_sf(crs=crs_proj,

           expand=TRUE) +
  guides(colour=guide_legend(override.aes=list(size=3, alpha=1))) +
  theme(axis.text=element_blank(), axis.ticks=element_blank(),

  labs(title=paste0("GFW fishing events by year (sample of ", sample_size_yr, " per year)"),
       subtitle="ICES 27.4.C / 27.7.D / 27.7.E,  Internal waters excluded") +

```

### 4.5.3 Kernel density in the study area

Kernel density estimation (KDE) converts the discrete set of fishing event locations into a continuous surface representing the spatial intensity of fishing effort. For each year, fishing event coordinates are projected into a metric coordinate system (UTM zone 30N) and a Gaussian kernel with bandwidth σ = `r sigma_all/1000` km is applied within the study area boundary (land excluded). The resulting density surface is normalised within each year to a 0–1 scale, where 1 represents the grid cell with the highest density and 0 the lowest. This within-year normalisation makes annual maps directly comparable in terms of spatial pattern, but means that absolute effort levels cannot be compared between years, a year with low total effort and a year with high total effort will both have cells reaching 1.0. For absolute effort comparisons, refer to Figures 10 and 11.

The KDE maps corroborate and sharpen the patterns visible in the point distribution maps above. The persistent high-density hotspot in the southern North Sea (27.4.C) along the Dutch and Belgian coasts is clearly visible throughout the series, with the peak density area appearing to shift and compress progressively eastward over time, consistent with the displacement effect of expanding wind farm developments. In the Channel, the eastern entrance to 27.7.D around the Pas de Calais consistently shows the highest effort density, reflecting the concentration of French bottom trawl activity in this area. A notable feature emerging from around 2021–2022 is the relative weakening of the 27.7.E density signal, particularly in the northern (UK) portion of the division, reinforcing the post-Brexit reduction in UK fleet activity suggested by the point maps. The KDE representation also makes clear that while the spatial footprint of fishing appears broadly stable across the series, the intensity within hotspot areas has increased relative to background effort levels — a pattern that will be quantified further by the concentration metrics in the following section.

```{r gfw-plot-kde, fig.height=10, fig.cap=fig_nums("kde_all")}
ggplot() +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_tile(data=kde_results, aes(x=x, y=y, fill=ndensity)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option="inferno", name="Relative\ndensity",
                       limits=c(0,1), breaks=c(0,0.5,1),
                       labels=c("Low","Mid","High"), na.value="transparent") +
  geom_sf(data=world_proj, fill="grey85", colour="grey60", linewidth=0.2) +
  geom_sf(data=fao_div_proj, fill=NA, colour="grey30", linewidth=0.4) +
  coord_sf(crs=crs_proj,
           xlim=st_bbox(study_window_proj)[c("xmin","xmax")],
           ylim=st_bbox(study_window_proj)[c("ymin","ymax")],
           expand=TRUE) +
  theme(axis.text=element_blank(), axis.ticks=element_blank(),
        axis.title=element_blank(), legend.position="bottom",
        strip.background=element_rect(fill="grey90"),
        strip.text=element_text(face="bold", colour="grey20")) +
  labs(title=paste0("GFW: Fishing effort density, all fleets (σ = ", sigma_all/1000, " km)"),
       subtitle="Normalised per year  —  Land excluded") +
  facet_wrap(~year, ncol=3)
```

### 4.5.4 Kernel density in ICES 27.7.D

The eastern Channel (ICES 27.7.D) is the division of primary interest for the *flyshoot* fishery and is examined in more detail using a finer kernel bandwidth of σ = `r sigma_7d/1000` km, which resolves spatial structure at a scale more appropriate for within-division analysis. The estimation window is restricted to 27.7.D, with internal waters excluded, and the density surface is again normalised within each year to a 0–1 scale to allow direct comparison of spatial patterns across years independently of changes in total effort.

The 27.7.D KDE maps reveal a persistent concentration of effort in the eastern portion of the division, centred on the Pas de Calais and the Baie de Seine. This hotspot is visible throughout the series and reflects the sustained intensity of French OTB activity in these historically important grounds. Effort in the western portion of 27.7.D is consistently lower, with UK effort progressively weakening from around 2021, reinforcing the pattern identified in the full-area maps and the point distribution figures. The finer bandwidth makes the spatial sharpness of the hotspot clearer: rather than a broad gradient of effort, there is a pronounced peak in the east that becomes relatively more dominant over time, consistent with the increasing concentration metrics presented in the following section.


```{r gfw-plot-kde-7d, fig.height=10, fig.cap=fig_nums("kde_7d")}
bbox_7d <- fao_div_proj |>
  filter(division == "27.7.D") |>
  st_bbox()

ggplot() +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_tile(data = kde_7d, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = ndensity)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option   = "inferno", name = "Relative\ndensity",
                       limits   = c(0, 1), breaks = c(0, 0.5, 1),
                       labels   = c("Low", "Mid", "High"),
                       na.value = "transparent") +
  geom_sf(data = world_proj,   fill = "grey85", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = fao_div_proj, fill = NA,       colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.4) +
  coord_sf(crs    = crs_proj,
           xlim   = bbox_7d[c("xmin", "xmax")],
           ylim   = bbox_7d[c("ymin", "ymax")],
           expand = TRUE) +
  theme(axis.text  = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        axis.title = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "grey20")) +
  labs(title    = paste0("GFW: Fishing effort density ICES 27.7.D (σ = ",
                          sigma_7d/1000, " km)"),
       subtitle = "Normalised per year  —  Internal waters and land excluded") +
  facet_wrap(~year, ncol = 3)

```



## 4.6 GFW effort spatial concentration in 27.7.D: Gini coefficient and top-10% cell share

Two complementary metrics are used to quantify the spatial concentration of fishing effort across the `r cell_size/1000` km × `r cell_size/1000` km grid cells covering ICES 27.7.D.

The **Gini coefficient** is a standard inequality measure borrowed from economics, adapted here to quantify the unevenness of effort across grid cells. It ranges from 0 to 1: a value of 0 means fishing effort is spread perfectly uniformly across all cells; a value of 1 means all effort is concentrated in a single cell. In practice, fishing effort is always somewhat concentrated. Values above 0.7 indicate strong spatial concentration in a small number of areas, while values below 0.5 suggest a relatively dispersed fleet. A rising Gini over time indicates that the fleet is progressively concentrating in fewer locations.

The **top-10% cell share** is a more intuitive companion metric: it asks what percentage of the total annual fishing events falls within the 10% of grid cells that were most intensively fished that year. If effort were uniform, this would be exactly 10%. In practice values of 40–70% are common in concentrated fisheries, meaning that a small fraction of the available sea area absorbs the majority of fishing pressure. Together, the two metrics capture different aspects of spatial concentration: the Gini summarises the full distribution of effort, while the top-10% share focuses specifically on the most intensively exploited areas.

Both metrics indicate a moderate but meaningful increase in spatial concentration of fishing effort in ICES 27.7.D over the study period. The Gini coefficient rose from 0.53–0.57 in 2013–2016 to 0.60–0.66 in 2019–2025, suggesting progressive compression of effort into a smaller number of grid cells. The top-10% cell share tells a similar story: the proportion of total effort in the most-fished 10% of cells increased from around 34–40% in the early period to a peak of 50% in 2020, before partially stabilising at 41–44% in recent years. Together these metrics quantify what the KDE maps suggested qualitatively — that while the broad spatial footprint of fishing in the eastern Channel has remained relatively stable, effort has become increasingly concentrated within already-intensively-fished areas. The peak in concentration around 2019–2020 coincides with a period of significant fleet restructuring driven by post-Brexit access uncertainty and the COVID19 pandemic. The partial relaxation of concentration since 2021 may reflect fleets settling into new access arrangements under the EU-UK TCA, though values remain consistently above the pre-2018 baseline, pointing to a structural rather than purely temporary shift in spatial behaviour.

```{r gfw-plot-concentration, fig.height=4, fig.cap=fig_nums("concentration")}
p_gini <- ggplot(concentration_7d, aes(x=year, y=gini)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_line(colour="#E15759", linewidth=1) + geom_point(colour="#E15759", size=3) +
  geom_text(aes(label=round(gini,2)), vjust=-0.8, size=2.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=study_years) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,1), labels=scales::number_format(accuracy=0.01)) +
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, vjust=0.5)) +
  labs(x="", y="Gini coefficient", title="Gini coefficient")

p_top10 <- ggplot(concentration_7d, aes(x=year, y=top10_pct)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_line(colour="#4E79A7", linewidth=1) + geom_point(colour="#4E79A7", size=3) +
  geom_text(aes(label=paste0(round(top10_pct,0),"%")), vjust=-0.8, size=2.8) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=study_years) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,NA), expand=expansion(mult=c(0,0.15)),
                     labels=scales::percent_format(scale=1)) +
  theme(axis.text.x=element_text(angle=90, vjust=0.5)) +
  labs(x="", y="% of total effort", title="Top-10% cell share")

p_gini + p_top10 +
  plot_annotation(
    title    = paste0("GFW: Effort concentration ICES 27.7.D  —  ",
                      cell_size/1000, " km grid  —  All fleets"),
    subtitle = "Left: Gini coefficient (0=uniform, 1=fully concentrated). Right: % effort in top-10% cells.")

```

The per-country KDE maps for ICES 27.7.D confirm that French effort dominates this division throughout all three periods, accounting for approximately 69–74% of GFW fishing days. The UK fleet contributes around 15–17%, with a modest decline in the most recent period (2022–2025) consistent with post-Brexit access restructuring. Belgian and Dutch effort in 27.7.D is substantially lower in absolute terms — around 6% and 5% respectively — meaning that on the shared colour scale used in the figure, these fleets appear dark not because of absence of fishing activity but because their effort density is an order of magnitude lower than the French fleet. The spatial patterns for the UK fleet show a broad distribution across the western portion of the division, while Dutch effort is more concentrated in the eastern Channel near the Pas de Calais, consistent with the flyshoot operational area documented in Brunel et al. (2025).

```{r gfw-plot-kde-7d-country, fig.height=10, fig.width=6, fig.cap=fig_nums("kde_7d_country")}

kde_flags   <- c("FRA", "GBR", "NLD", "BEL")

# Define periods — labels and year ranges
kde_periods <- list(
  "2013\u20132018" = 2013:2018,
  "2019\u20132021" = 2019:2021,
  "2022\u20132025" = 2022:2025
)

# Filter events to 27.7.D and relevant flags, derive year
events_7d <- events_classified_fr |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(lubridate::year(start))) |>
  filter(division    == "27.7.D",
         vessel_flag %in% kde_flags,
         year        %in% unlist(kde_periods))

# Project to UTM30N
events_7d_sf <- events_7d |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("lon", "lat"), crs = 4326) |>
  st_transform(crs_proj)

# Compute KDE per period × flag — pool all years within each period
kde_7d_grid <- expand.grid(
    period = names(kde_periods),
    flag   = kde_flags,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ) |>
  purrr::pmap_dfr(function(period, flag) {
    yrs <- kde_periods[[period]]
    pts <- events_7d_sf |>
      filter(vessel_flag == flag,
             year        %in% yrs)
    if (nrow(pts) < 20) return(NULL)

    coords  <- st_coordinates(pts)
    ppp_obj <- spatstat.geom::ppp(
      x      = coords[, 1],
      y      = coords[, 2],
      window = study_owin
    )
    kde_raw <- spatstat.explore::density.ppp(
      ppp_obj,
      sigma    = sigma_7d,
      dimyx    = c(200, 200),
      positive = TRUE
    )
    as.data.frame(kde_raw) |>
      rename(density = value) |>
      mutate(period      = period,
             vessel_flag = flag)
  })

# Normalise within each period column (shared scale per period)
# so that relative country contributions are visible across rows
kde_7d_grid <- kde_7d_grid |>
  group_by(period) |>
  mutate(ndensity = (density - min(density, na.rm = TRUE)) /
                   (max(density, na.rm = TRUE) - min(density, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(vessel_flag = factor(vessel_flag, levels = kde_flags),
         period      = factor(period,      levels = names(kde_periods)))

# Crop to 27.7.D bounding box
bbox_7d <- fao_div_proj |>
  filter(division == "27.7.D") |>
  st_bbox()

ggplot() +
  geom_tile(data = kde_7d_grid,
            aes(x = x, y = y, fill = ndensity)) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    option   = "inferno",
    name     = "Relative density",
    limits   = c(0, 1),
    breaks   = c(0, 0.5, 1),
    labels   = c("Low", "Mid", "High"),
    na.value = "transparent"
  ) +
  geom_sf(data = world_proj,   fill = "grey85",
          colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = fao_div_proj, fill = NA,
          colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.4) +
  coord_sf(crs    = crs_proj,
           xlim   = bbox_7d[c("xmin", "xmax")],
           ylim   = bbox_7d[c("ymin", "ymax")],
           expand = TRUE) +
  facet_grid(period ~ vessel_flag) +
  labs(
    title    = paste0("GFW: Fishing effort density ICES 27.7.D by country and period",
                      " (\u03c3 = ", sigma_7d / 1000, " km)"),
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Periods: ", paste(names(kde_periods), collapse = ", "),
      "  \u2014  Density normalised within each period\n",
      "Colour scale is shared across countries within each period,",
      " reflecting relative fleet contributions"
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text        = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks       = element_blank(),
        axis.title       = element_blank(),
        legend.position  = "bottom",
        legend.key.width = unit(2, "cm"),
        strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90"),
        strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9))
```

## 4.4 Channel fisheries context: literature review

This section places the quantitative results from Sections 4.1–4.6 in the broader context of the Channel fisheries literature. It draws on ICES WGCSE, STECF, Ifremer, MMO and peer-reviewed sources (see Section 3.5 for the literature selection approach).

### 4.4.1 Fleet composition and dominant gear types

The Channel (ICES 27.7.d/e) supports one of the most diverse and intensively fished areas in Europe. The French fleet dominates total effort in the eastern Channel, contributing over 60% of total AER fishing days in most years (ICES, 2025a; Ifremer, 2026), consistent with the AER results in Figure 1 which show France as the largest contributor across all gear categories. Bottom trawl/seine gears account for the largest share of demersal fishing effort, targeting mixed assemblages of flatfish, cephalopods and small pelagics. The Dutch flyshoot fleet expanded  through the 2010s (Quirijns et al., 2020), a trend visible in the AER and GFW series (Figures 1 and 10). Belgian beam trawl effort has declined substantially since the mid-2000s under pressure from fuel costs and quota restrictions (ILVO, 2022), consistent with the low and declining Belgian effort in beam trawl panels throughout the AER figures.

The scallop dredge fishery is concentrated in the Baie de Seine (27.7.d) and western Channel (27.7.e), dominated by the French fleet with seasonal UK participation. Scallop landings from the Baie de Seine reached a record ~48,000 t in 2024–2025 (Ifremer, 2025). MSC certification has been granted for the Baie de Saint-Brieuc fishery (2022) and the Baie de Seine fishery (November 2024), covering the majority of French Channel scallop production (MSC, 2024). The AER landings data (Figures 5–7) confirm scallops as one of the highest-tonnage species in the study area, dominated by the French dredge fleet.

Pot and trap fisheries targeting whelk (*Buccinum undatum*), crab and lobster are important to UK coastal communities, though the AER series shows limited representation of this segment at the fleet level. The whelk fishery in 27.7.d has grown markedly since the mid-2010s, driven by Asian export demand (MMO, 2023).

### 4.4.2 Historical effort trends and structural change

Total fishing effort in the Channel has declined substantially since the early 2000s, consistent with EU fleet capacity reduction programmes and quota restrictions under successive CFP reforms. The AER series (2008–2023) shows a general downward trend in fishing days for bottom trawl/seine and beam trawl across all major countrys (Figure 1), with the Dutch flyshoot fleet being an important exception showing growth through the 2010s before stabilising post-2020. This is consistent with Quirijns et al. (2020) and STECF (2024).

Post-Brexit disruption from 2021 onwards has reshaped fleet access in the eastern Channel. UK licensing restrictions have reduced French, Belgian and Dutch access to UK waters in 27.7.d/e, driving spatial redistribution towards French EEZ waters (Phillipson & Symes, 2018; House of Lords, 2022). This structural shift may contribute to the apparent changes in spatial effort patterns visible in the GFW KDE maps (Figures 14–15) around 2021–2022, with effort concentrating in the southern (French EEZ) portion of 27.7.d. Post-Brexit bilateral agreements and access negotiations between the EU member states and the UK continue to shape fleet access patterns in the Channel.

The GFW spatial concentration metrics (`r fig_nums("concentration", display="cite")`) quantify whether this redistribution has led to more or less concentrated effort patterns over time. An increase in Gini coefficient and top-10% share after 2021 is consistent with effort being pushed into a narrower range of spatial locations following access restrictions.

### 4.4.3 Stock status of key target species

Table 2 summarises the assessment and advice status for the principal commercial stocks in the study area. Stocks are grouped by the ICES working group responsible for their assessment. Note that several species caught in the Channel, particularly cephalopods, do not have formal ICES assessments or TAC-based management; these are indicated accordingly.

### 4.4.4 Ecosystem effects and sustainability

The seabed disturbance footprint of the Channel fisheries has been extensively studied. Eigaard et al. (2017) quantified the swept-area ratio across European shelf fisheries and identified the Channel as one of the most intensively bottom-trawled areas in European waters, with beam trawl having the highest physical impact per unit effort. Comparisons between gear types consistently show that Danish seine (flyshoot) has a substantially lower seabed disturbance footprint than comparable otter trawls or beam trawls, primarily because it does not drag heavy groundgear across the seabed in the same manner (Depestele et al., 2016; Hiddink et al., 2017). 

Bycatch and discards in the Channel mixed fisheries remain a management concern under the EU landing obligation (in force since 2019), though exemptions for high-survival species and *de minimis* provisions have reduced the practical scope of the obligation for many fleets (ICES WGCSE, 2025a). The flyshoot fishery is generally considered to have moderate bycatch rates compared to other demersal gears, though species composition of the bycatch varies considerably with area and season (Quirijns et al., 2020).


# 5. Discussion & Synthesis

## 5.1 Effort trends and fleet position

Total fishing effort in the Channel (ICES 27.4.c/27.7.d/27.7.e) has declined substantially over the 2008–2023 period covered by the AER series, with a reduction of approximately 30% across all gears and countries combined. This decline is consistent with the long-term trend of EU fleet capacity reduction under successive CFP reform cycles, and with the structural contraction of the Belgian and Dutch beam trawl segments visible in both landings and effort data. France dominates the total effort picture throughout, contributing around 80% of fishing days, and its otter trawl (OTB) fleet in the eastern Channel shows a steady but gradual decline over the period. Landings of key species have also declined: flatfish landings fell by over 60% since 2008, consistent with poor stock status for Channel sole and plaice, while scallop landings increased markedly since 2016. The FDI-based gear disaggregation, which is only available from 2013 onwards, shows that within the declining bottom trawl/seine category the gear composition has remained broadly stable over the 2013–2023 sub-period.

The Dutch flyshoot (SSC/SDN) fleet presents a contrasting trajectory: although small in absolute days relative to the French OTB fleet, it has been relatively stable and seine-dominated, with the FDI gear split confirming that roughly 70% of Dutch bottom trawl/seine days in the Channel are attributable to seine gears. This fleet segment is small in AER terms but disproportionately visible in the GFW spatial data because of the high AIS coverage on the larger vessel segments. .

Post-Brexit restructuring from 2021 onwards has had a measurable effect on spatial distribution. The GFW annual maps show a progressive reduction in UK effort in 27.7.e and a sharpening of national spatial separation from 2021, consistent with altered access conditions under the Trade and Cooperation Agreement (European Commission, 2021). The Dutch fleet in 27.4.C shows spatial compression that could at least partly be attributable to the ongoing expansion of offshore wind farm development zones, which are progressively reducing the navigable fishing area available to trawling and seine vessels (Quirijns et al., 2020).

## 5.2 Comparison of AER and GFW effort metrics

The AER and GFW series measure effort using fundamentally different methodologies: administrative logbook declarations versus AIS-derived vessel-day estimates. Therefore, they are not directly comparable in absolute terms. The GFW series shows an increasing trend from 53,000 to 90,000 days over 2013–2025, while the AER shows a declining trend over 2013–2023. These opposing directions are reconciled by three structural factors: improving AIS coverage over the early years of the GFW series inflates apparent growth; GFW includes the UK fleet (contributing ~25–30% of total days) which is absent from the AER series; and GFW captures large vessels with high AIS compliance most accurately, while the AER captures the full administrative fleet including small inshore vessels below the AIS carriage threshold.

The most useful role of the GFW data in this report is therefore not as an independent cross-check of absolute effort levels, but as a source of spatial resolution unavailable from the AER. The within-division distribution of effort, the identification of national fishing grounds, and the detection of temporal shifts in spatial patterns can be based on GFW data. Used in this complementary way, the two sources are mutually reinforcing: the AER provides the authoritative time series of effort and landings by fleet segment, while GFW provides the spatial context that the AER cannot. The FDI was retained for the methodologically important role of gear-code disaggregation of the AER bottom trawl/seine category, but its quality limitations (confidentiality suppression, EU-aggregated landings) precluded its use as a primary effort or landings source (STECF, 2025b).

## 5.3 Compliance with management measures and bilateral agreements

Direct assessment of compliance with effort and gear management measures is beyond the scope of this report, which relies on aggregated AER and GFW data rather than vessel-level logbook or VMS records. However, the data presented allow some observations relevant to the monitoring context. The GFW spatial concentration metrics in 27.7.D show a step increase in Gini coefficient and top-10% cell share from 2018–2020 onwards, which coincides with the period of increasing negotiation pressure around Brexit access arrangements. This pattern is consistent with a progressive restriction of vessel access to previously used grounds, whether through formal licensing or informal avoidance. The partial reduction in concentration since 2022 may reflect stabilisation of access arrangements under the TCA, though concentration remains structurally elevated above pre-2018 levels.

The FDI gear split confirms that the Dutch fleet's contribution to bottom trawl/seine effort in the Channel is predominantly seine (*flyshoot*), providing a quantitative baseline against which future changes in gear composition — for example in response to gear specifications in bilateral agreements — could be assessed. Across all fleets, conventional bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB) accounts for approximately 57% of bottom trawl/seine fishing days, with seine (SSC/SDN) accounting for around 10%, reflecting the much larger scale of the French OTB fleet relative to the Dutch seine fleet. More granular vessel-level monitoring would be required to assess day-level compliance with any sea-day limits. The AER and GFW data presented here operate at fleet-segment and annual resolution and are best suited to detecting structural trends rather than real-time compliance monitoring.

# 6. Conclusions & Recommendations

## 6.1 Conclusions

This report has characterised fishing effort, landings and spatial distribution in the English Channel and southern North Sea (ICES 27.4.c/27.7.d/27.7.e) over the period 2008–2023 (AER), 2013–2023 (FDI) and 2013–2025 (GFW), integrating three complementary data sources.

Total fishing effort has declined by approximately 30% since 2008, driven primarily by contraction of French otter trawl and Belgian and Dutch beam trawl effort. France dominates total effort throughout, contributing around 80% of AER fishing days. The Dutch flyshoot fleet, while small in absolute days, is the dominant seine fleet in the area and has remained relatively stable, although it should be noted that the AER data does not provide information on the UK-flagged fleet, which may also be important to consider. Landings are dominated by flatfishes, scallops and shrimps; flatfish landings have declined markedly, consistent with the deteriorating stock status of Channel sole and plaice (ICES, 2025a; ICES, 2025b). Scallop landings show an increasing trend since 2016, supported by record biomass in the Baie de Seine (Varenne & Foucher, 2025).

GFW spatial analysis reveals persistent fishing hotspots in the Pas de Calais and Baie de Seine, with Dutch effort in 27.4.C showing progressive spatial compression likely linked to wind farm expansion. Post-Brexit spatial restructuring is visible from 2021, with declining UK effort in 27.7.e and increased spatial separation between national fleets. Spatial concentration in 27.7.D — as measured by the Gini coefficient and top-10% cell share — has increased from a pre-2018 baseline and remains elevated, pointing to a structural rather than temporary shift in spatial behaviour.

The FDI-based gear-code disaggregation shows that across all fleets, conventional bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB) accounts for approximately 57% of bottom trawl/seine fishing days in the study area, with seine gears (SSC/SDN, predominantly Dutch) accounting for around 10%. The Dutch fleet is distinct in being predominantly seine-dominated (~70% of Dutch bottom trawl/seine days), while the French fleet is almost entirely OTB (~96%). This baseline characterisation provides the quantitative foundation against which future fleet developments and the effects of access agreements can be assessed.

Silverman, B. W. (1986). *Density Estimation for Statistics and Data Analysis*. Chapman and Hall, London.

STECF (2025a). *STECF 25-07: EU Fleet Economic and Transversal data (AER)*. Scientific, Technical and Economic Committee for Fisheries, European Commission. https://stecf.jrc.ec.europa.eu/

STECF (2025b). *STECF 25-10: Fisheries Dependent Information (FDI)*. Scientific, Technical and Economic Committee for Fisheries, European Commission. https://stecf.jrc.ec.europa.eu/


# Annexes

## Annex A — Data sources

| Dataset | Source | Period | Role in this report |
|---------|--------|--------|---------------------|
| STECF AER | STECF 25-07 | 2008–2023 | Primary: effort trends, landings |
| GFW Events API | GFW API v3 (`gfwr` 3.0) | 2013–2025 | Spatial analysis only |
| GFW Vessel registry | GFW | 2013–2025 | Flag, gear type, GT |
| STECF FDI | STECF 2025 release | 2013–2024 | QA reference only |
| ICES FAO shapefiles | ICES/FAO | — | ICES division polygons |

## Annex B — Cache files

Cache files are stored in `output/cache/` and are rebuilt automatically when source data are newer. Delete any file to force a full rebuild on the next knit.

| File | Contents | Rebuilt when |
|------|----------|--------------|
| `cache_aer.RData` | `aer_effort_raw`, `aer_effort_summary`, `aer_effort_capacity_metric`, `aer_landings_raw`, `aer_landings_summary` | AER Excel file is newer |
| `cache_gfw.RData` | `fishing_days_study`, `events_classified_fr`, `vessel_meta`, `fao_sf_division`, `world` | Any GFW pipeline `.RData` is newer |
| `cache_gfw_spatial.RData` | KDE grids, gridded effort, concentration metrics | `cache_gfw.RData` is newer |
| `cache_fdi.RData` | `fdi_days`, `fdi_catches` | FDI CSV outputs are newer |

## Annex C — Code section index

The table below maps each result in the report to the R code chunk or script section that generated it. All chunk names refer to `channel_fisheries_combined_report.Rmd` unless otherwise stated.

Development of the R analysis code and report structure was supported in part by Claude (Anthropic, 2025), a large language model AI assistant. The AI assisted with data processing pipeline development, figure code, and drafting of text sections. All analytical decisions, interpretations and conclusions are the responsibility of the author.

| Figure / Table | Report section | Code chunk / script section | Source data |
|----------------|---------------|------------------------------|-------------|
| Figure 1 — Fishing days by gear | 4.2.1 | `aer-effort-trend` | `aer_effort_summary` (cache_aer) |
| Figure 2 — Fishing days by vessel size | 4.2.2 | `aer-effort-gt` | `aer_effort_raw` (cache_aer) |
| Figure 3 — Seasonal patterns | 4.2.3 | `aer-effort-seasonal` | `aer_effort_summary` (cache_aer) |
| Figure 4 — Landed weight by gear | 4.3.1 | `aer-landings-total` | `aer_landings_summary` (cache_aer) |
| Figure 5 — Landings by species and country | 4.3.2 | `aer-landings-species-country` | `aer_landings_summary` (cache_aer) |
| Figure 6 — Landings by species and gear | 4.3.3 | `aer-landings-species-gear` | `aer_landings_summary` (cache_aer) |
| Figure 7 — Focal species × focal gears | 4.3.4 | `aer-landings-focal` | `aer_landings_summary` (cache_aer) |
| Figure 8 — Top 15 species | 4.3.5 | `aer-landings-top-species` | `aer_landings_summary` (cache_aer) |
| Figure 10 — GFW days by country | 4.4.1 | `gfw-plot-flag-total` | `fishing_days_study` (cache_gfw) |
| Figure 11 — AER vs GFW comparison | 4.4.2 | `aer-gfw-comparison` | `aer_effort_summary` + `fishing_days_study` |
| Figure 12 — Spatial events, all years | 4.5.1 | `gfw-plot-spatial-all` | `events_classified_fr`, `vessel_meta` (cache_gfw) |
| Figure 13 — Spatial events by year | 4.5.2 | `gfw-plot-spatial-by-year` | `events_classified_fr`, `vessel_meta` (cache_gfw) |
| Figure 14 — KDE all divisions | 4.5.3 | `gfw-plot-kde` | `kde_results` (cache_gfw_spatial) |
| Figure 15 — KDE ICES 27.7.D | 4.5.4 | `gfw-plot-kde-7d` | `kde_7d` (cache_gfw_spatial) |
| Figure 16 — Gini and top-10% | 4.6.1 | `gfw-plot-concentration` | `concentration_7d` (cache_gfw_spatial) |
| Table 1 — FDI exclusion summary | 3.4 | `fdi-note-table` | Hard-coded |
| Table 2 — Stock status | 4.7.3 | Markdown table (no chunk) | ICES 2025a–e (literature) |

**KDE computation** (`kde_results`, `kde_7d`): derived in the `load-gfw-spatial` chunk using `spatstat::density.ppp()` with bandwidth σ = `r sigma_all/1000` km (all divisions) and σ = `r sigma_7d/1000` km (27.7.D). Inputs are fishing event coordinates from `events_classified_fr`, sampled to `r kde_sample` events per year.

**Concentration metrics** (`concentration_7d`): derived in `load-gfw-spatial` by aggregating events to a `r cell_size/1000` km × `r cell_size/1000` km grid covering ICES 27.7.D, then computing the Gini coefficient (`ineq::Gini()`) and top-10% cell share per year.

**GFW pipeline scripts** (not part of this Rmd — run separately to regenerate the raw `.RData` files in `flyshootdir`):

| Script / Rmd | Purpose | Output file |
|---|---|---|
| `GFW_effort_report.Rmd` sections 1–3 | Vessel discovery and metadata | `gfw_s3_vessel_meta.RData` |
| `GFW_effort_report.Rmd` sections 4–6 | Event retrieval and zone classification | `gfw_s6_zones.RData` |
| `GFW_effort_report.Rmd` section 7 | Effort aggregation to vessel-days | `gfw_s7_effort.RData` |
| `AER_channel_analysis.R` | AER exploration and QA plots | (diagnostic output only) |
| `FDI_channel_analysis.R` | FDI loading, cleaning, QA | `fdi_fishingdays_*.csv`, `fdi_catches_*.csv` |



## Annex D — Supplementary figures

The tables below summarise the key data extracted from the STECF AER and FDI datasets for the study area (ICES 27.4.c/27.7.d/27.7.e), covering the period `r aer_years_start`–`r aer_years_end`. Values are rounded for presentation; totals may not sum exactly due to rounding. All weights in tonnes (live weight); effort in fishing days.

### Table D1. Total landed weight (t) by country and year — all gears

```{r annex-d1, echo=FALSE}
make_annex_table(
  df         = aer_landings_summary |>
                 filter(sub_reg %in% study_divisions_aer,          # no country filter here
                        year    %in% aer_years_start:aer_years_end),
  row_var    = "year",     col_var   = "country_code",
  value_var  = "live_weight_t",
  row_label  = "Year",    col_levels = report_countries_aer,       # helper lumps the rest
  add_other  = TRUE,
  caption    = tab_nums("annex_d1",
    paste0("Total landed weight (t) by year and country, all gears, ",
           "ICES 4.c/7.d/7.e (AER, ", aer_years_start, "\u2013", aer_years_end, ")."))
)

```

  # filter(species_group=="Other") %>%

### Table D6. FDI gear split: fishing days by country and gear code (bottom trawl/seine only)

Based on `aer_split` — the FDI-derived disaggregation of the AER `Bottom trawl/seine` category. Only direct FDI splits shown (pooled fallback rows excluded). Countries with fewer than 100 total split days excluded. See Section 3.4 for methodology.

```{r annex-d6, echo=FALSE}
if (!is.null(aer_split)) {
  make_annex_table(
    df         = aer_split |>
                   filter(split_source == "FDI direct",
                          year         %in% aer_years_start:aer_years_end),
    row_var    = "year",  col_var   = "gear_type",
    value_var  = "totfishdays_split",
    row_label  = "Year",
    col_levels = c("Bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB)", "Seine (SSC/SDN)"),
    add_other  = TRUE,
    caption    = tab_nums("annex_d6",
      paste0("FDI gear-code split: fishing days by year and gear type for bottom ",
             "trawl/seine (AER + FDI direct splits, ",
             aer_years_start, "\u2013", aer_years_end,
             "). 'Other' = pooled fallback or unsplit strata."))
  )
} else {
  cat("aer_split not available.\n")
}
```

### Table D7. Total fishing days by gear and year — focused gears with bottom trawl/seine split

Bottom trawl/seine disaggregated into bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB) and seine (SSC/SDN) using FDI split key. Other focused gears shown as reported in AER.

```{r annex-d7, echo=FALSE}
gear_order <- c("Bottom trawl/seine (unsplit)",
                "Bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB)",
                "Seine (SSC/SDN)",
                setdiff(capacity_gears, "Bottom trawl/seine"))

# Block 1: pre-2013 — BTS unsplit, other gears normal
pre2013_bts <- aer_effort_summary |>
  filter(sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
         gear_category == "Bottom trawl/seine",
         year          %in% aer_years_start:2012) |>
  group_by(year, gear_category) |>
  summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  rename(gear_label = gear_category) |>
  mutate(gear_label = "Bottom trawl/seine (unsplit)")

pre2013_other <- aer_effort_summary |>
  filter(sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
         gear_category %in% capacity_gears,
         gear_category != "Bottom trawl/seine",
         year          %in% aer_years_start:2012) |>
  group_by(year, gear_category) |>
  summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  rename(gear_label = gear_category)

# Block 2: 2013+ — BTS split via FDI, other gears normal
post2013_bts <- if (!is.null(aer_split)) {
  aer_split |>
    filter(year      %in% 2013:aer_years_end,
           gear_type != "Unsplit") |>
    group_by(year, gear_type) |>
    summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays_split, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
    rename(gear_label = gear_type)
} else {
  aer_effort_summary |>
    filter(sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
           gear_category == "Bottom trawl/seine",
           year          %in% 2013:aer_years_end) |>
    group_by(year, gear_category) |>
    summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
    rename(gear_label = gear_category) |>
    mutate(gear_label = "Bottom trawl/seine (unsplit)")
}

post2013_other <- aer_effort_summary |>
  filter(sub_reg       %in% study_divisions_aer,
         gear_category %in% capacity_gears,
         gear_category != "Bottom trawl/seine",
         year          %in% 2013:aer_years_end) |>
  group_by(year, gear_category) |>
  summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  rename(gear_label = gear_category)

all_data <- bind_rows(pre2013_bts, pre2013_other,
                      post2013_bts, post2013_other) |>
  mutate(totfishdays = round(totfishdays)) |>
  group_by(year, gear_label) |>
  summarise(totfishdays = sum(totfishdays, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from  = gear_label,
              values_from = totfishdays,
              values_fill = NA) |>
  dplyr::select(year, any_of(gear_order)) |>
  arrange(year) |>
  mutate(Total = rowSums(across(any_of(gear_order)), na.rm=TRUE))

# Build total row separately on the completed data frame
total_row <- all_data |>
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) sum(x, na.rm=TRUE))) |>
  mutate(year = NA_integer_)

# Bind and convert year to character
all_data <- bind_rows(all_data, total_row) |>
  mutate(year = if_else(is.na(year), "Total", as.character(year)))

# Convert NA to "--" for display (must be character columns)
all_data_display <- all_data |>
  mutate(across(any_of(gear_order),
                \(x) if_else(is.na(x), "--", formatC(x, format="d", big.mark=","))))

# Rename year column
names(all_data_display)[1] <- "Year"

# Build flextable
ft <- flextable::flextable(all_data_display) |>
  style_ft(font_size = 8) |>
  # Right-align numeric-looking columns (all except Year)
  flextable::align(j = -1, align = "right", part = "all") |>
  flextable::align(j = 1,  align = "left",  part = "all") |>
  # Shade pre-2013 rows slightly to signal unsplit period
  flextable::bg(i = ~ Year %in% as.character(aer_years_start:2012),
                j = c("Bottom trawl (OTB/OTT/PTB)", "Seine (SSC/SDN)"),
                bg = "#EEEEEE") |>
  flextable::set_caption(
    caption = tab_nums("annex_d7",
      paste0("Total fishing days by year and gear, with bottom trawl/seine ",
             "disaggregated using the FDI gear-code split from 2013 onwards. ",
             "'--' indicates gear not separately reported for that year. ",
             "ICES 4.c/7.d/7.e (AER + FDI, ",
             aer_years_start, "\u2013", aer_years_end, ")."))
  )

ft
```
